files..github/review-gate.yml:
# Settings for the review gate (.github/scripts/review_gate.py). Every value
# starts at the gate's default; delete a line to keep the default.
# Unknown keys and bad values fail the gate instead of being ignored.
# The workflows read this file from the PR's base branch, so a PR cannot
# change the settings its own review runs under.

# The "Review gate" check is always reported. "two" also keeps the older
# "Claude On-Demand" check up to date, for branch rules that still require
# it; "one" once they require "Review gate" alone.
checks: one

# The runner label (runs-on) for the review jobs; several labels, comma
# separated, pick a self-hosted runner ("self-hosted, linux"). Run such a
# runner under an account of its own with no Claude Code setup: the
# reviewers load that account's user settings, hooks and instructions, and
# the review installs Claude Code into its home folder.
runner: ubuntu-latest

# The review that runs on every PR with reviewable files. Its backup runs
# once when the attempts on its own model fail, a usage limit included.
routine:
  model: claude-fable-5-1
  effort: low
  max_turns: 120
  fallback_model: claude-opus-5-5
  fallback_effort: high

# The deeper review the routine one asks for on risky diffs.
deep:
  model: claude-fable-5-1
  effort: low
  max_turns: 120
  fallback_model: claude-opus-5-5
  fallback_effort: high

# The backup a tier uses when its own fallback_model or fallback_effort
# line is left out.
fallback:
  model: claude-opus-5-5
  effort: high

# A folder of the project's own pre-screen checks (*.py and *.sh), run from
# the base branch with the changed-file list; their output joins the review
# context, and a check that exits non-zero is reported as a violation.
# A check that runs the PR's code can fake its own report, and on a
# self-hosted runner that is not wiped between jobs it can leave files or
# processes behind for the review; keep such checks on hosted or one-job
# runners. Empty: none.
# attribution: on scans the lines a PR adds for AI-attribution markers
# (co-author lines, "generated with" footers, vendor links), and the
# reviewer checks the commits and the PR body for them; off skips both.
prescreen:
  dir:
  attribution: on

# The project's own deep-review triggers, on top of the gate's: path globs
# (comma separated, any case; `*` crosses folders, a trailing `/` covers a
# folder), and a Python regex matched against the lines a PR adds (no `#`,
# which starts a comment here; one pair of outer quotes is dropped, so wrap a
# regex that starts and ends with the same quote in another pair). They
# apply to PRs the gate reviews: a PR of only skippable files (Markdown,
# images, fonts outside the always-reviewed paths) passes without a review,
# so a trigger on such a file never fires; list its path under
# triage.always_review too. Empty: none.
# auto: on lets the routine review ask for the deep review by itself: on
# these triggers, on the gate's own files, and when it judges one needed.
# off: it starts none by itself and the triggers are not used; a person
# asks for one with `@claude review this PR` on each push that needs it,
# or adds the needs-deep-review label so every later push gets one.
escalate:
  auto: on
  paths:
  patterns:

# Paths that always get a review, whatever their file type, on top of the
# gate's own (.github/scripts/, .github/review-guide.md, any .claude/
# folder, any CLAUDE.md): globs as for escalate.paths. Without this, a PR
# of only Markdown, images or fonts passes without a review.
triage:
  always_review:

# Extra tools both reviewers may use, comma separated: Bash(...) patterns,
# Read, Grep or Glob. A Bash pattern that runs the PR's code hands that code
# the review's tokens; add one only when that is acceptable. Empty: none.
reviewer:
  allowed_tools:
files..github/review-guide.md:
# Review guide

The project's own part of the review prompt. Both review tiers read this file from the PR's base branch, so a PR cannot change the guide its own review follows, and every change to it gets a review.

## About this project

**claude-code-templates**: {{ONE_LINE_DESCRIPTION}}

## Project invariants to verify (in priority order)

Replace these starting points with the rules a change here must never break, highest risk first.

1. **Contract stability**: public APIs, file formats and schemas change only on purpose, with every caller and stored file still handled.
2. **Shared code**: a change to a shared utility keeps working for every caller, not only the one the PR needed.
3. **Tests earn their place**: a new test that misses rules 1 to 3 of `.claude/rules/testing.md` § When a test earns its place is a blocking finding.
4. **Clean code**: a breach of `.claude/rules/clean-code.md` (history or planning codes in comments, cryptic names, copied helpers) in lines the PR adds or changes is a blocking finding.

## Also escalate when the diff includes

These escalate on their own: the gate's own files (`.github/scripts/**`, `.github/review-gate.yml`, this guide, the review workflows and the project's check folder) and the trigger paths and patterns in `.github/review-gate.yml` (`escalate.*`). List here the changes that need a reviewer's judgment to spot, for example:

- Changes to how data is saved or loaded
- New code on a trust boundary (user input, network, plugins)
files..github/scripts/review_gate.py:
"""The review gate's logic, shared by the routine and deep review workflows so
the workflow files stay the same for every project. Standard library and the
runner's `gh`, Python 3.8+. The workflows run the copy from the base branch.

    review_gate.py triage FILES [--incomplete] [--file .github/review-gate.yml]
        -> {"review": true|false}
    review_gate.py verdict --since TS (--tier routine --marker RE | --tier deep)
        -> {"verdict": "pass"|"block"|"missing", "line": ...[, "recovered": ...]}
        (reads the PR's comments as `gh api --paginate` prints them, on stdin)
    review_gate.py gate --state STATE [--triage T] [--routine R] [--escalated] [--deep D] [--order O]
        -> {"status", "conclusion", "title", "summary", "state"} for the "Review gate" check
    review_gate.py upsert --repo OWNER/NAME --sha HEAD [facts as for gate] [--note TEXT]
        -> the same, after creating or updating the check on that commit (GH_TOKEN
           needs checks: write); --note is appended to the check's summary, and
           --order is required with --triage, --routine or --deep
    review_gate.py settings [--file .github/review-gate.yml] -> KEY=value lines
        (dots become underscores; runner_labels adds the runner as a JSON list)
    review_gate.py escalate FILES DIFF [--file .github/review-gate.yml]
        -> {"escalate": true|false, "paths": [...], "lines": [...]}, the
           project's own deep-review triggers met by the changed files (one
           per line in FILES) and the lines the diff in DIFF adds

The "Review gate" check carries its own state in its external_id, e.g.
"triage=reviewable;routine=pass;escalated=yes;deep=none;routine_by=0.0.0;deep_by=0.0.0"
(an empty one is the start state). Each review workflow reads it, sets the
facts it knows and writes back the result, so whichever finishes last has
every fact. T: reviewable|skip; R: pending|pass|block|missing|error;
D: none|pass|block|missing|error. --escalated only ever turns on: once a deep
review was asked for, it stays asked. A workflow that cannot tell a fact
leaves its option out, keeping the stored value.

The two workflows can write at the same moment, and a write carries the whole
state as its writer read it, so one can wipe the other's facts. Two rules make
that harmless:
  - Each tier's facts carry the --order of the step that wrote them,
    RUN.ATTEMPT.STEP (routine_by for triage and routine, deep_by for deep),
    compared as numbers, field by field. RUN is whatever makes the run that
    counts the newest within its tier: the routine workflow uses its run id,
    and the deep workflow uses the moment its review job started, in
    nanoseconds, since its newest run cancels the one in flight. The two tiers'
    stamps are never compared with each other. A write from an older run never
    replaces a newer run's facts, so a cancelled deep run cannot undo the run
    that replaced it.
  - After writing, upsert reads the check back twice, a few seconds apart, and
    writes again when its own facts are gone.

Every command prints one line; a bad argument prints {"error": ...} and exits 1.
"""

import fnmatch
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

# Never reviewed: the review action refuses to run on a PR whose copy of the
# review workflow differs from the default branch's, so a workflow-only PR has
# to pass as non-reviewable. Only that one workflow: claude.yml (the deep tier
# runs the default branch's copy), any other workflow, and a script or action
# kept under .github/workflows/ are reviewed like any other file. A .yaml twin
# would run as a separate workflow, so it is reviewed too.
NEVER = re.compile(r"^\.github/workflows/claude-code-review\.yml$")
# Skipped only when every other path is Markdown, an image or a font that is
# not always reviewed. Always reviewed, whatever the file type, in every
# project: .github/scripts/, where a file Python loads before the standard
# library could run in the gate; .github/review-guide.md, the project's part
# of both review prompts; and a .claude/ folder at any depth and any
# CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md, the instructions and skills both review tiers
# load (Claude Code reads a subfolder's when it reads files there). A project
# adds its own paths with `triage.always_review` in the gate settings. Matched
# in any case, as a case-insensitive checkout would place the file. Anything
# else gets a review: scripts, config, lockfiles, an SVG, which can carry
# script, and a .gitattributes or .lfsconfig.
SKIPPABLE = re.compile(r"\.(md|png|jpe?g|gif|webp|ico|ttf|otf|woff2?)$", re.I)
ALWAYS_REVIEWED = re.compile(r"^\.github/scripts/|^\.github/review-guide\.md$|(^|/)\.claude/"
                             r"|(^|/)CLAUDE(\.local)?\.md$", re.I)

# The files API stops at 3,000 entries: a listing that long may be cut short.
LISTING_CAP = 3000

GATE = "Review gate"
BOT = "claude[bot]"
# A deep verdict comment: the review action's finished tracking comment, or
# the comment the CLI run on the API credits posts under this heading.
DEEP_MARKER = re.compile(r"\A(\*\*Claude finished|## Deep review)")
# Bot comments that are never a routine verdict: the deep-review request and
# the review action's tracking comments ("Claude Code is working…" while it
# runs, "**Claude finished…**" or "**Claude encountered an error**" after),
# whose glyphs belong to other runs, and a deep review whose heading is
# written slightly off ("# Deep Review", "**Deep review**").
NOT_ROUTINE = re.compile(r"\A(@claude review this PR|\*\*Claude |Claude Code is working"
                         r"|[#*_\s]*deep review)", re.I)
GLYPHS = re.compile("🔴|🟢")
# A line that blocks wherever it sits. Each prefix reads a checkbox ("[ ]",
# "[x]") as one unit and any other non-letter as another, never both ways,
# so a long row of checkboxes cannot make the match backtrack.
# 1. A 🔴 after list, quote, table, heading or emphasis markup: "**🔴 …**",
#    "- 🔴 x", "1. 🔴 Blocking …". Prose naming a 🔴 keeps it in backticks.
RED_OPENER = re.compile(r"(?:\[[ xX]\]|(?!\[[ xX]\]|[`🔴🟢])[\W\d_])*🔴")
# 2. "Blocking" opening a line after the same markup, as written when the
#    glyph is dropped: "1. **Blocking** — …", "### Blocking issues", "_Blocking_".
BLOCKING = re.compile(r"(?:\[[ xX]\]|(?!\[[ xX]\]|[`🟢])[\W\d_])*(?:Blocking|BLOCKING)(?![^\W_])")
# 3. "Blocking" right after a short label: up to 30 characters (a
#    single-backtick code span counts as one; a longer backtick run ends
#    the label) ending in a colon, a dash or a 🔴. After a
#    colon any case counts ("**Verdict:** blocking"). After a dash or a 🔴,
#    "Blocking" and "BLOCKING" always count ("- `a.py:1` — Blocking: x"),
#    and a lower-case "blocking" counts unless a word or a code span
#    follows it, which makes it an adjective in prose ("Change 3 — blocking
#    output", "— blocking `wait()`"); "— blocking finding" and "— blocking
#    issue" still count. A hyphen right after a letter or digit joins a
#    word ("Non-blocking: none") and ends no label.
_AFTER_LABEL = r"(?:(?![`🟢])[\W\d_])*"
# A word or a code span after the lower-case word, other than "finding" or
# "issue", even behind emphasis or a bracket ("— blocking **I/O**",
# "— blocking (sync) writes").
_ADJECTIVE = r"\s+[*_(\[~]*(?!(?i:findings?|issues?)(?![^\W_]))(?:[^\W_]|`)"
LABEL = re.compile(r"(?:(?<![`\\])`[^`]+`(?!`)|[^`🔴🟢]){0,30}?"
                   r"(?:[:：]" + _AFTER_LABEL + r"(?i:Blocking)"
                   r"|(?:[—–−]|(?<![^\W_])[-‐‑]|🔴)" + _AFTER_LABEL
                   + r"(?:Blocking|BLOCKING|(?i:blocking)(?![^\W_])(?!" + _ADJECTIVE + r")))"
                   r"(?![^\W_])")
# The verdict is the last line, under the review action's footer. Only lines
# that say nothing are skipped: a rule line, or an optional rule then pieces
# joined by "·" or "•", each empty or one item after an optional "branch:":
# a job or branch link on GitHub, or a branch name in a code span (no space
# or other character git refuses in a branch name). A lone item needs a
# "branch:" or "[View job]" in front ("[View job](…) · Branch: [`b`](…)",
# "--- · `b`"). Any words on a trailing line make it the last line.
FOOTER_RULE = re.compile(r"(?:-{3,}|\*{3,}|_{3,})")
_BRANCH = r"[^`\s~^:?*\[\\\]🔴🟢]{1,200}"
FOOTER_ITEM = re.compile(r"(?:[Bb]ranch:?\s*)?(?:\[(?:View job|`?%s`?)\]\(https://github\.com/"
                         r"[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+/(?:tree|actions/runs)/[^\s)🔴🟢]*\)|`%s`)" % (_BRANCH, _BRANCH))
FOOTER_LONE = re.compile(r"[Bb]ranch|\[View job\]")


def _footer(line):
    rest = line.strip()
    rule = FOOTER_RULE.match(rest)
    if rule:
        rest = rest[rule.end():].strip()
    if not rest:
        return True
    parts = re.split("[·•]", rest)
    return (all(not p.strip() or FOOTER_ITEM.fullmatch(p.strip()) for p in parts)
            and (len(parts) > 1 or bool(FOOTER_LONE.match(rest))))
# A quoted line ("> 🟢 LGTM") is someone else's verdict, never this one.
VERDICT_LINE = re.compile(r"[\s#*_]*(?:🔴|🟢)")
VERDICTS = ("pass", "block", "missing", "error")
STATE_VALUES = {
    "triage": ("reviewable", "skip"),
    "routine": ("pending",) + VERDICTS,
    "escalated": ("no", "yes"),
    "deep": ("none",) + VERDICTS,
}
START_STATE = {"triage": "reviewable", "routine": "pending", "escalated": "no", "deep": "none",
               "routine_by": "0.0.0", "deep_by": "0.0.0"}
# The order field that stamps each tier's facts, and the form of an order.
OWNER = {"triage": "routine_by", "routine": "routine_by", "deep": "deep_by"}
ORDER = re.compile(r"[0-9]{1,20}\.[0-9]{1,4}\.[0-9]{1,2}")
# upsert reads its write back after each of these delays, and writes again
# when its facts are gone, at most WRITE_ROUNDS times in all.
SETTLE_SECONDS = (3, 10)
WRITE_ROUNDS = 3

DEFAULTS = {
    "checks": "one", "runner": "ubuntu-latest",
    "routine.model": "claude-fable-5-1", "routine.effort": "low", "routine.max_turns": "120",
    "routine.fallback_model": "claude-opus-5-5", "routine.fallback_effort": "high",
    "deep.model": "claude-fable-5-1", "deep.effort": "low", "deep.max_turns": "120",
    "deep.fallback_model": "claude-opus-5-5", "deep.fallback_effort": "high",
    "fallback.model": "claude-opus-5-5", "fallback.effort": "high",
    "prescreen.dir": "", "prescreen.attribution": "on",
    "escalate.auto": "on", "escalate.paths": "", "escalate.patterns": "", "reviewer.allowed_tools": "",
    "triage.always_review": "",
}
SECTIONS = {k.split(".")[0] for k in DEFAULTS if "." in k}
# A tier's own backup, when its file leaves it out, follows the shared one.
TIER_FALLBACK = {"%s.fallback_%s" % (t, k): "fallback." + k for t in ("routine", "deep") for k in ("model", "effort")}
_LABEL = r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}"
_GLOB = r"[A-Za-z0-9._/*?-]{1,200}"
_TOOL = r"(?:Bash\([^\"'`$\\(),\n]{1,200}\)|Read|Grep|Glob)"
CHECKS = {
    "checks": re.compile(r"one|two"),
    "runner": re.compile(r"%s(?:, *%s){0,7}" % (_LABEL, _LABEL)),
    "model": re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,63}"),
    "effort": re.compile(r"low|medium|high|xhigh|max"),
    "max_turns": re.compile(r"[1-9][0-9]{0,2}"),
    # A folder in the repo, relative, with no `..` part.
    # The first character is no `-`, so no tool reads the value as an option.
    "dir": re.compile(r"|(?!(?:.*/)?\.\.(?:/|$))[A-Za-z0-9._][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}"),
    "paths": re.compile(r"|%s(?:, *%s){0,49}" % (_GLOB, _GLOB)),
    "always_review": re.compile(r"|%s(?:, *%s){0,49}" % (_GLOB, _GLOB)),
    # Any Python regex up to 500 characters; settings() also compiles it.
    "patterns": re.compile(r"[^\n]{0,500}"),
    "allowed_tools": re.compile(r"|%s(?:, *%s){0,19}" % (_TOOL, _TOOL)),
    "attribution": re.compile(r"on|off"),
    "auto": re.compile(r"on|off"),
}
CHECKS["fallback_model"], CHECKS["fallback_effort"] = CHECKS["model"], CHECKS["effort"]


class GateError(Exception):
    pass


def triage(paths, incomplete=False, always_review=""):
    """Whether a diff with these changed paths gets an AI review.
    `always_review` is the project's `triage.always_review` setting."""
    if incomplete or len(paths) >= LISTING_CAP:
        return True
    globs = _globs(always_review)
    return any(not NEVER.search(p) and (ALWAYS_REVIEWED.search(p) or _glob_match(p, globs)
                                        or not SKIPPABLE.search(p)) for p in paths)


def _globs(setting):
    return [g.strip().casefold() for g in setting.split(",") if g.strip()]


def _glob_match(path, globs):
    """A path setting's match: any case, `*` crosses folders, and a glob
    ending in `/` covers the folder."""
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path.casefold(), g + "*" if g.endswith("/") else g) for g in globs)


def _comments(text):
    """Every comment in `gh api --paginate` output, which prints one JSON array per page."""
    decoder, out, i = json.JSONDecoder(), [], 0
    while True:
        while i < len(text) and text[i].isspace():
            i += 1
        if i == len(text):
            return out
        page, i = decoder.raw_decode(text, i)
        if not isinstance(page, list):
            raise GateError("the comments are not a JSON list")
        out.extend(page)


def _bot_bodies(text, since):
    return [c.get("body") or "" for c in _comments(text)
            if isinstance(c, dict) and (c.get("user") or {}).get("login") == BOT
            and (c.get("created_at") or "") >= since]


def _pick(bodies, tier, marker):
    """The newest comment of `tier`. A routine comment carries `marker`, its
    heading: a comment without one is never taken for the routine verdict,
    since deep runs and requests post glyphs into the same thread. It is never
    a deep comment, even one quoting the routine review, nor a request or
    tracking comment that names the heading."""
    if tier == "deep":
        found = [b for b in bodies if DEEP_MARKER.search(b)]
    else:
        found = [b for b in bodies if marker.search(b) and not DEEP_MARKER.search(b)
                 and not NOT_ROUTINE.search(b)]
    return found[-1] if found else None


def _line(body):
    """The verdict line: the last line under the action's footer, which must
    open with 🔴 or 🟢; any 🔴 on it blocks. A line that blocks wherever it
    sits (RED_OPENER, BLOCKING, LABEL) blocks whatever the verdict line says:
    a 🟢 after it ("once fixed, this is 🟢 LGTM", a "🟢 All clear on X"
    heading) must not pass it, and the glyph is what gets dropped. With any
    other last line, a 🔴 on the last line holding a glyph blocks; otherwise
    the verdict is missing: a bare "LGTM", or "Verdict = Blocking" under a
    "🟢 All clear on X" heading, never passes."""
    lines = body.splitlines()
    glyph = any("🔴" in l or "🟢" in l for l in lines)
    early = next(((l, how) for l in lines for how, rule in
                  (("red-over-glyph", RED_OPENER), ("word-over-glyph", BLOCKING), ("word-over-glyph", LABEL))
                  if rule.match(l)), None)
    while lines and _footer(lines[-1]):
        lines.pop()
    last = lines[-1].strip() if lines else ""
    if VERDICT_LINE.match(last) and "🔴" in last:
        return "block", last, "glyph"
    if early:
        line, how = early
        return "block", line.strip(), (how if glyph else "word")
    if VERDICT_LINE.match(last):
        return "pass", last, "glyph"
    # No verdict line, but the last line holding a glyph holds a 🔴 ("Verdict:
    # 🔴 the writer races", then a closing remark): a block, never a missing
    # verdict, which would start a second deep review that could bury it.
    marked = [l for l in lines if "🔴" in l or "🟢" in l]
    if marked and "🔴" in marked[-1]:
        return "block", marked[-1].strip(), "glyph"
    return "missing", "", ""


def verdict(text, since, tier, marker=None):
    """The verdict in the bot's newest comment of `tier` posted at or after
    `since`. A block read from a "Blocking" line rather than a 🔴 adds
    `recovered`."""
    body = _pick(_bot_bodies(text, since), tier, re.compile(marker) if marker else None)
    if body is None:
        return {"verdict": "missing", "line": ""}
    result, line, how = _line(body)
    out = {"verdict": result, "line": line}
    if how == "word":
        out["recovered"] = "no 🔴/🟢 line; a line opening with Blocking"
    elif how == "word-over-glyph":
        out["recovered"] = "a line opening with Blocking outranks the 🟢 line"
    elif how == "red-over-glyph":
        out["recovered"] = "a line opening with 🔴 outranks the later 🟢 line"
    return out


def _check(status, conclusion, title, summary):
    return {"status": status, "conclusion": conclusion, "title": title, "summary": summary}


FAILED = {
    "block": ("Blocked by the {} review", "The {} review found something to fix. Fix it on the PR branch and push."),
    "missing": ("No {} verdict", "The {} review finished without a 🟢 or 🔴 line. Re-run it."),
    "error": ("The {} review errored", "No {} review attempt ran to the end. Re-run it."),
}


def _failed(result, tier):
    title, summary = FAILED[result]
    return _check("completed", "failure", title.format(tier), summary.format(tier))


def decide(triage_result, routine=None, escalated=False, deep=None):
    """The "Review gate" check from everything known so far. Both review
    workflows call this with the same facts, so whichever finishes last
    writes the full answer. Fails closed: anything but a clean pass from
    every tier that ran, or was asked for, blocks the merge."""
    if deep not in (None, "pass"):
        return _failed(deep, "deep")
    if triage_result == "skip":
        if deep == "pass":
            return _check("completed", "success", "Deep review 🟢", "The diff has no reviewable files and the deep review passed.")
        if escalated:
            return _check("in_progress", None, "Deep review in progress", "A deep review was asked for on a diff with no reviewable files.")
        return _check("completed", "success", "No review needed", "The diff has no reviewable files.")
    if routine == "pending":
        return _check("in_progress", None, "Routine review in progress", "Waiting for the routine review's verdict.")
    if routine != "pass":
        return _failed(routine, "routine")
    if deep == "pass":
        return _check("completed", "success", "Routine and deep reviews 🟢", "Both review tiers passed.")
    if escalated:
        return _check("in_progress", None, "Deep review in progress", "The routine review passed and asked for a deep review.")
    return _check("completed", "success", "Routine review 🟢", "The routine review passed and asked for no deep review.")


def parse_state(text):
    """The gate state stored in the check's external_id; empty is the start state."""
    state = dict(START_STATE)
    for part in filter(None, text.split(";")):
        key, _, value = part.partition("=")
        if key in OWNER.values():
            ok = ORDER.fullmatch(value)
        else:
            ok = value in STATE_VALUES.get(key, ())
        if not ok:
            raise GateError("bad gate state: " + part)
        state[key] = value
    return state


def _order(text):
    return tuple(int(p) for p in text.split("."))


def gate(state_text, triage=None, routine=None, escalated=False, deep=None, order=None):
    """Set the facts this workflow knows on the stored state, then decide.
    With `order`, a tier's facts are set only when no newer run wrote them."""
    state = parse_state(state_text)
    if order is not None and not ORDER.fullmatch(order):
        raise GateError("--order must be RUN.ATTEMPT.STEP, three numbers")
    for key, value in (("triage", triage), ("routine", routine), ("deep", deep)):
        if value is None:
            continue
        _choice(value, STATE_VALUES[key], "--" + key)
        if order is not None:
            if _order(order) < _order(state[OWNER[key]]):
                continue
            state[OWNER[key]] = order
        state[key] = value
    if escalated:
        state["escalated"] = "yes"
    check = decide(state["triage"], state["routine"], state["escalated"] == "yes",
                   None if state["deep"] == "none" else state["deep"])
    check["state"] = ";".join("%s=%s" % (k, state[k]) for k in START_STATE)
    return check


def _gh(path, method="GET", body=None):
    cmd = ["gh", "api", path, "-X", method] + (["--input", "-"] if body is not None else [])
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, input=json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None,
                       capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode:
        raise GateError("gh api %s %s failed: %s" % (method, path, r.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()))
    return json.loads(r.stdout.decode("utf-8") or "null")


def check_body(check, note=""):
    """The Checks API body for a gate decision."""
    body = {"status": check["status"], "external_id": check["state"],
            "output": {"title": check["title"], "summary": (check["summary"] + " " + note).strip()}}
    if check["conclusion"]:
        body["conclusion"] = check["conclusion"]
    return body


def _newest(repo, sha):
    runs = _gh("repos/%s/commits/%s/check-runs?check_name=Review%%20gate&per_page=100" % (repo, sha))
    mine = [r for r in runs.get("check_runs", []) if r.get("name") == GATE]
    return max(mine, key=lambda r: r["id"]) if mine else None


def _write(repo, sha, current, note, facts):
    check = gate((current or {}).get("external_id") or "", **facts)
    body = check_body(check, note)
    if current:
        _gh("repos/%s/check-runs/%d" % (repo, current["id"]), "PATCH", body)
    else:
        _gh("repos/%s/check-runs" % repo, "POST", dict(body, name=GATE, head_sha=sha))
    return check


def _holds(current, facts):
    """Whether the check still has this write's facts, or a newer run's
    facts for the same tier."""
    if current is None:
        return False
    state = parse_state(current.get("external_id") or "")
    if facts.get("escalated") and state["escalated"] != "yes":
        return False
    for key in OWNER:
        if facts.get(key) is None:
            continue
        stored, mine = _order(state[OWNER[key]]), _order(facts["order"])
        if stored < mine or (stored == mine and state[key] != facts[key]):
            return False
    return True


def upsert(repo, sha, note="", **facts):
    """Decide from the gate check's stored state plus `facts`, then write the
    result back to the check on `sha`, creating it on the first call. Reads
    it back, and writes again while another workflow's write wiped the facts."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+", repo) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", sha):
        raise GateError("upsert needs --repo OWNER/NAME and a 40-character --sha")
    if facts.get("order") is None and any(facts.get(k) is not None for k in OWNER):
        raise GateError("upsert needs --order with --triage, --routine or --deep")
    check = _write(repo, sha, _newest(repo, sha), note, facts)
    for round_ in range(WRITE_ROUNDS):
        current = None
        for delay in SETTLE_SECONDS:
            time.sleep(delay)
            current = _newest(repo, sha)
            if not _holds(current, facts):
                break
        else:
            return check
        if round_ < WRITE_ROUNDS - 1:
            check = _write(repo, sha, current, note, facts)
    raise GateError("another workflow kept overwriting the Review gate; re-run this job")


def settings(text):
    """KEY=value pairs from review-gate.yml: top-level keys and one level of
    nesting, `#` comments. Unknown keys and bad values are errors, never ignored."""
    values, section, given = dict(DEFAULTS), None, set()
    for n, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        line = raw.split("#", 1)[0].rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        m = re.fullmatch(r"( *)([a-z_]+):\s*(.*)", line)
        if not m:
            raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: expected `key: value`" % n)
        indent, key, value = m.groups()
        if not indent and not value:
            if key not in SECTIONS:
                raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: %s needs a value" % (n, key) if key in DEFAULTS
                                else "review-gate.yml line %d: unknown section %s" % (n, key))
            section = key
            continue
        name = "%s.%s" % (section, key) if indent else key
        if indent and section is None:
            raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: indented key outside a section" % n)
        if name not in DEFAULTS:
            raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: unknown setting %s" % (n, name))
        value = value.strip()
        # One matching pair of outer quotes, never more: a regex may start or
        # end with a quote of its own.
        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in "\"'":
            value = value[1:-1]
        elif value[:1] in ("\"", "'"):
            # An opening quote with no partner: a `#` inside quotes cut the
            # value short, and keeping the rest would change its meaning.
            raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: unbalanced quote in %s (a `#` starts a comment)" % (n, name))
        if not CHECKS[name.split(".")[-1]].fullmatch(value) or not _compiles(name, value):
            raise GateError("review-gate.yml line %d: bad value for %s: %s" % (n, name, value))
        values[name] = value
        given.add(name)
        section = section if indent else None
    for name, shared in TIER_FALLBACK.items():
        if name not in given:
            values[name] = values[shared]
    return values


def _compiles(name, value):
    if name != "escalate.patterns":
        return True
    try:
        re.compile(value)
    except re.error:
        return False
    return True


HUNK = re.compile(r"@@ -\d+(?:,(\d+))? \+\d+(?:,(\d+))? @@")


def added_lines(diff):
    """The lines a unified diff adds, read hunk by hunk with the counts in
    each `@@` header, so an added line that starts with `++` (`++i;`) is never
    taken for a `+++` file header."""
    added, old, new = [], 0, 0
    for line in diff.split("\n"):
        if old <= 0 and new <= 0:
            m = HUNK.match(line)
            if m:
                old, new = int(m.group(1) or 1), int(m.group(2) or 1)
            continue
        if line.startswith("+"):
            # One trailing CR is the file's CRLF ending, dropped so a
            # `$`-anchored pattern still matches; a CR inside the line stays.
            added.append(line[1:-1] if line.endswith("\r") else line[1:])
            new -= 1
        elif line.startswith("-"):
            old -= 1
        elif not line.startswith("\\"):
            old, new = old - 1, new - 1
    return added


def escalate(paths, added, values):
    """The project's own deep-review triggers from review-gate.yml: paths that
    match an `escalate.paths` glob (any case; `*` crosses folders, and a glob
    ending in `/` covers the folder), and added diff lines that
    `escalate.patterns` finds. Returns what matched, so the pre-screen can
    name it. Nothing matches while `escalate.auto` is off: the project then
    asks for every deep review by hand."""
    if values["escalate.auto"] == "off":
        return {"escalate": False, "paths": [], "lines": []}
    globs = _globs(values["escalate.paths"])
    pattern = re.compile(values["escalate.patterns"]) if values["escalate.patterns"] else None
    hits = [p for p in paths if _glob_match(p, globs)]
    lines = [line for line in added if pattern.search(line)] if pattern else []
    return {"escalate": bool(hits or lines), "paths": hits, "lines": lines[:20]}


def _option(args, name, default=None):
    if name not in args:
        return default
    i = args.index(name) + 1
    if i == len(args):
        raise GateError(name + " needs a value")
    return args[i]


def _choice(value, allowed, name):
    if value not in allowed:
        raise GateError("%s must be one of %s" % (name, ", ".join(allowed)))
    return value


def run(argv):
    cmd, args = (argv[0], argv[1:]) if argv else ("", [])
    if cmd == "triage" and args:
        with open(args[0], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            paths = [l.strip() for l in fh if l.strip()]
        values = _settings_file(args[1:])
        return {"review": triage(paths, "--incomplete" in args, values["triage.always_review"])}
    if cmd == "verdict":
        since = _option(args, "--since")
        tier = _choice(_option(args, "--tier"), ("routine", "deep"), "--tier")
        marker = _option(args, "--marker")
        if not since or (tier == "routine") != bool(marker):
            raise GateError("verdict needs --since, and --marker exactly when --tier is routine")
        # Bytes, not text: the verdict emoji must not depend on the runner's locale.
        return verdict(sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8"), since, tier, marker)
    if cmd in ("gate", "upsert"):
        facts = {"triage": _option(args, "--triage"), "routine": _option(args, "--routine"),
                 "escalated": "--escalated" in args, "deep": _option(args, "--deep"),
                 "order": _option(args, "--order")}
        if cmd == "upsert":
            return upsert(_option(args, "--repo", ""), _option(args, "--sha", ""), _option(args, "--note", ""), **facts)
        if "--state" not in args:
            raise GateError("gate needs --state (an empty one is the start state)")
        return gate(_option(args, "--state"), **facts)
    if cmd == "settings":
        return _settings_file(args)
    if cmd == "escalate" and len(args) >= 2:
        values = _settings_file(args[2:])
        # Names decode strictly, as for triage: a name that is not UTF-8 fails
        # the command (one error line) rather than its printing.
        with open(args[0], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            paths = [p for p in fh.read().split("\n") if p]
        # newline="": a carriage return inside an added line must stay in it,
        # not split it into a line with no "+" that the hunk walk skips.
        with open(args[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as fh:
            added = added_lines(fh.read())
        return escalate(paths, added, values)
    raise GateError("Usage: see the top of .github/scripts/review_gate.py")


def _settings_file(args):
    path = _option(args, "--file", ".github/review-gate.yml")
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text = fh.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        text = ""
    return settings(text)


def main(argv):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        result = run(argv)
    except (GateError, OSError, ValueError) as e:
        print(json.dumps({"error": str(e)}))
        return 1
    if argv and argv[0] == "settings":
        labels = [label.strip() for label in result["runner"].split(",")]
        lines = ["%s=%s" % (k.replace(".", "_"), v) for k, v in result.items()]
        print("\n".join(lines + ["runner_labels=" + json.dumps(labels)]))
    else:
        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sets up what the review gate needs on a GitHub repository: the
# needs-deep-review label, merge settings, a ruleset per protected branch
# that requires the "Review gate" check, the review token secret, and the
# Claude GitHub App. With --check it changes nothing: it reports every
# missing piece and exits 1 when any is missing.
#
# Needs the gh CLI, logged in with admin access to the repository. Run it
# from the repository folder, or pass --repo OWNER/NAME.

set -euo pipefail

# GitHub Actions: the app that reports the workflows' checks.
readonly ACTIONS_APP_ID=15368
readonly LABEL="needs-deep-review"
readonly TOKEN_SECRET="CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"
readonly KEY_SECRET="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
# Kept current only under `checks: two` in .github/review-gate.yml. Under
# `checks: one` nothing reports it, so a branch rule requiring it blocks
# every PR.
readonly OLD_DEEP_CHECK="Claude On-Demand"
readonly BRANCH_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$'
readonly CHECK_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9 ._,()/:+-]+$'

MODE=setup
REPO=""
BRANCHES=()
REQUIRED=("Review gate")
MERGE_STYLE=merge
APPROVALS=0
DEFAULT_BRANCH=""
GATE_CHECKS=one
GAPS=0

usage() {
  cat << 'EOF'
Usage: setup-review-gate.sh [--check] [options]

  --check              Report what is missing and change nothing. Exits 1
                       when anything is missing.
  --repo OWNER/NAME    The repository (default: the one in this folder).
  --branch NAME        A branch to protect; repeat for more (default: the
                       default branch, plus develop when it exists).
  --require NAME       Another check the branches require besides
                       "Review gate"; repeat for more.
  --merge-style STYLE  merge, squash or rebase (default: merge).
  --approvals N        Approvals a PR needs besides the gate, 0 to 9
                       (default: 0, for a single maintainer).
EOF
}

die() {
  echo "error: $*" >&2
  exit 2
}

ok() { printf '  ok       %s\n' "$*"; }
fixed() { printf '  set up   %s\n' "$*"; }
note() { printf '  note     %s\n' "$*"; }
missing() {
  printf '  MISSING  %s\n' "$*"
  GAPS=$((GAPS + 1))
}

parse_args() {
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --check) MODE=check ;;
      --repo) REPO=${2:?--repo needs OWNER/NAME}; shift ;;
      --branch) BRANCHES+=("${2:?--branch needs a name}"); shift ;;
      --require) REQUIRED+=("${2:?--require needs a check name}"); shift ;;
      --merge-style) MERGE_STYLE=${2:?--merge-style needs a value}; shift ;;
      --approvals) APPROVALS=${2:?--approvals needs a number}; shift ;;
      -h | --help) usage; exit 0 ;;
      *) usage >&2; die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done
  validate_args
}

# Names end up inside jq programs and JSON text, so anything that could
# break out of a quoted string is refused.
validate_args() {
  local name repo_re='^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$'
  case "$MERGE_STYLE" in
    merge | squash | rebase) ;;
    *) die "--merge-style takes merge, squash or rebase" ;;
  esac
  [[ $APPROVALS =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || die "--approvals takes a number from 0 to 9"
  [[ -z $REPO || $REPO =~ $repo_re ]] || die "--repo takes OWNER/NAME"
  for name in ${BRANCHES[@]+"${BRANCHES[@]}"}; do
    [[ $name =~ $BRANCH_RE ]] || die "unsupported branch name: $name"
  done
  for name in "${REQUIRED[@]}"; do
    [[ $name =~ $CHECK_RE ]] || die "unsupported check name: $name"
  done
}

branch_exists() {
  gh api "repos/$REPO/branches/$1" --silent 2> /dev/null
}

preflight() {
  local admin
  command -v gh > /dev/null || die "the gh CLI is not installed"
  if [ -z "$REPO" ]; then
    REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) \
      || die "no GitHub repository here; pass --repo OWNER/NAME"
  fi
  admin=$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .permissions.admin) || die "cannot read $REPO"
  [ "$admin" = true ] || die "$REPO: reading and changing its settings needs admin access"
  DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .default_branch)
  if [ ${#BRANCHES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    BRANCHES=("$DEFAULT_BRANCH")
    if [ "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" != develop ] && branch_exists develop; then
      BRANCHES+=(develop)
    fi
  fi
}

# The `checks` setting from the repository's .github/review-gate.yml on its
# default branch; "one" when the file or the line is absent.
read_gate_checks() {
  local text value
  text=$(gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" \
    "repos/$REPO/contents/.github/review-gate.yml" 2> /dev/null) || text=""
  value=$(sed -nE 's/^checks:[[:space:]]*(one|two)([[:space:]#].*)?$/\1/p' <<< "$text")
  GATE_CHECKS=${value:-one}
}

step_label() {
  if gh api "repos/$REPO/labels/$LABEL" --silent 2> /dev/null; then
    ok "label $LABEL"
  elif [ "$MODE" = check ]; then
    missing "label $LABEL (the workflow adds it to PRs that owe a deep review)"
  else
    gh label create "$LABEL" -R "$REPO" --color B60205 \
      --description "The routine review asked for a deep review" > /dev/null
    fixed "label $LABEL"
  fi
}

# allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge for the style.
merge_flags() {
  case "$MERGE_STYLE" in
    merge) echo "true false false" ;;
    squash) echo "false true false" ;;
    rebase) echo "false false true" ;;
  esac
}

step_merge() {
  local want have m s r what="merge settings: $MERGE_STYLE only, branch deleted on merge"
  want="$(merge_flags) true"
  have=$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq '[.allow_merge_commit, .allow_squash_merge,
    .allow_rebase_merge, .delete_branch_on_merge] | map(tostring) | join(" ")')
  if [ "$have" = "$want" ]; then
    ok "$what"
  elif [ "$MODE" = check ]; then
    missing "$what"
  else
    read -r m s r <<< "$(merge_flags)"
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO" -F allow_merge_commit="$m" -F allow_squash_merge="$s" \
      -F allow_rebase_merge="$r" -F delete_branch_on_merge=true --silent
    fixed "$what"
  fi
}

step_secrets() {
  local names
  names=$(gh secret list -R "$REPO" --json name --jq '.[].name')
  if grep -qxF "$TOKEN_SECRET" <<< "$names"; then
    ok "secret $TOKEN_SECRET"
  elif [ "$MODE" = setup ] && [ -t 0 ]; then
    echo "  Paste the token that 'claude setup-token' prints:"
    gh secret set "$TOKEN_SECRET" -R "$REPO"
    fixed "secret $TOKEN_SECRET"
  else
    missing "secret $TOKEN_SECRET (get it with 'claude setup-token', then" \
      "run: gh secret set $TOKEN_SECRET -R $REPO)"
  fi
  if grep -qxF "$KEY_SECRET" <<< "$names"; then
    ok "secret $KEY_SECRET (reviews try the API credits first)"
  else
    note "no $KEY_SECRET secret: reviews run on the subscription only (optional)"
  fi
}

# A personal account gives gh no way to list installed apps, so the proof
# is a comment the app posted here, or an organization installation.
step_app() {
  local seen
  seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/comments?sort=created&direction=desc&per_page=100" \
    --jq '[.[] | select(.user.login == "claude[bot]")] | length')
  if [ "${seen:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    ok "Claude GitHub App (it has commented here)"
    return
  fi
  if [ "$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .owner.type)" = Organization ] \
    && gh api "orgs/${REPO%%/*}/installations" --jq '.installations[].app_slug' \
      2> /dev/null | grep -qx claude; then
    ok "Claude GitHub App (installed on the organization)"
    return
  fi
  note "Claude GitHub App not confirmed: install it from https://github.com/apps/claude" \
    "for $REPO, or run /install-github-app in Claude Code"
}

# A jq filter that is true when a ruleset is active and names the branch.
# Only exact names count, not patterns such as refs/heads/release/*.
covers_filter() {
  local ref="refs/heads/$1" default=""
  [ "$1" = "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ] && default=' or . == "~DEFAULT_BRANCH"'
  echo ".enforcement == \"active\" and .target == \"branch\"
    and ((.conditions.ref_name.include // []) | any(. == \"$ref\" or . == \"~ALL\"$default))
    and ((.conditions.ref_name.exclude // []) | index(\"$ref\") | not)"
}

# The repository's own rulesets that protect the branch, one id per line.
rulesets_for() {
  local id filter
  filter=$(covers_filter "$1")
  for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets?per_page=100" \
    --jq '.[] | select(.source_type == "Repository") | .id'); do
    if [ "$(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --jq "$filter")" = true ]; then
      echo "$id"
    fi
  done
}

# What the branch's rulesets lack, one line per gap; nothing when covered.
branch_gaps() {
  local ids id rule name types="" checks="" bypass=0
  ids=$(rulesets_for "$1")
  if [ -z "$ids" ]; then
    echo "no active ruleset"
    return
  fi
  for id in $ids; do
    types+=" $(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --jq '[.rules[].type] | join(" ")') "
    checks+=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --jq '.rules[]
      | select(.type == "required_status_checks")
      | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context')$'\n'
    bypass=$((bypass + $(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --jq '.bypass_actors | length')))
  done
  for rule in deletion non_fast_forward pull_request; do
    [[ $types == *" $rule "* ]] || echo "rule $rule"
  done
  for name in "${REQUIRED[@]}"; do
    grep -qxF "$name" <<< "$checks" || echo "required check \"$name\""
  done
  if [ "$GATE_CHECKS" = one ] && grep -qxF "$OLD_DEEP_CHECK" <<< "$checks"; then
    echo "drop required check \"$OLD_DEEP_CHECK\" (nothing reports it under checks: one)"
  fi
  [ "$bypass" -eq 0 ] || echo "no bypass actors (has $bypass)"
}

pr_rule() {
  echo "{\"type\": \"pull_request\", \"parameters\": {
    \"required_approving_review_count\": $APPROVALS, \"dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push\": true,
    \"require_code_owner_review\": false, \"require_last_push_approval\": false,
    \"required_review_thread_resolution\": false, \"allowed_merge_methods\": [\"$MERGE_STYLE\"]}}"
}

# The required checks as a JSON array, each reported by GitHub Actions.
checks_json() {
  local name sep="" out="["
  for name in "${REQUIRED[@]}"; do
    out+="$sep{\"context\": \"$name\", \"integration_id\": $ACTIONS_APP_ID}"
    sep=", "
  done
  echo "$out]"
}

new_ruleset() {
  cat << EOF
{"name": "$1-protection", "target": "branch", "enforcement": "active",
 "conditions": {"ref_name": {"include": ["refs/heads/$1"], "exclude": []}},
 "bypass_actors": [],
 "rules": [{"type": "deletion"}, {"type": "non_fast_forward"}, $(pr_rule),
   {"type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
     "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
     "required_status_checks": $(checks_json)}}]}
EOF
}

# A jq step that appends the rule ($2) when no rule of its type ($1) exists.
ensure_rule() {
  echo "(if any(.[]; .type == \"$1\") then . else . + [$2] end) |"
}

# A jq program that repairs a ruleset read from the API. "full" adds the
# missing rules and checks; "strip" only removes bypass actors and the old
# deep check, for the branch's other rulesets.
fix_filter() {
  local ensure="" add="[]" drop="." keep
  local no_checks='{"type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
    "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false, "required_status_checks": []}}'
  if [ "$1" = full ]; then
    ensure="$(ensure_rule deletion '{"type": "deletion"}')
      $(ensure_rule non_fast_forward '{"type": "non_fast_forward"}')
      $(ensure_rule pull_request "$(pr_rule)")
      $(ensure_rule required_status_checks "$no_checks")"
    add=$(checks_json)
  fi
  if [ "$GATE_CHECKS" = one ]; then
    drop="map(select(.context != \"$OLD_DEEP_CHECK\"))"
  fi
  # $have and $c are jq variables, not shell ones.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2016
  keep='. as $have | . + ['"$add"'[] | select(.context as $c | $have | all(.context != $c))]'
  echo "{name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors: [], rules: (.rules | $ensure
    map(if .type == \"required_status_checks\"
      then .parameters.required_status_checks |= ($drop | $keep) else . end))}"
}

apply_ruleset() {
  local ids id mode primary=""
  ids=$(rulesets_for "$1")
  if [ -z "$ids" ]; then
    new_ruleset "$1" | gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/rulesets" --input - --silent
    return
  fi
  # The full repair goes to the ruleset that already requires checks, so the
  # branch's other rulesets keep to their own purpose.
  for id in $ids; do
    if [ "$(gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" \
      --jq 'any(.rules[]; .type == "required_status_checks")')" = true ]; then
      primary=$id
      break
    fi
  done
  primary=${primary:-${ids%%$'\n'*}}
  for id in $ids; do
    mode="strip"
    if [ "$id" = "$primary" ]; then mode="full"; fi
    gh api "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --jq "$(fix_filter "$mode")" \
      | gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/rulesets/$id" --input - --silent
  done
}

step_rulesets() {
  local branch gaps gap
  for branch in "${BRANCHES[@]}"; do
    gaps=$(branch_gaps "$branch")
    if [ -n "$gaps" ] && [ "$MODE" = setup ]; then
      apply_ruleset "$branch"
      gaps=$(branch_gaps "$branch")
      [ -n "$gaps" ] || { fixed "ruleset on $branch"; continue; }
    fi
    if [ -z "$gaps" ]; then
      ok "ruleset on $branch"
      continue
    fi
    while IFS= read -r gap; do
      missing "ruleset on $branch: $gap"
    done <<< "$gaps"
  done
}

main() {
  parse_args "$@"
  preflight
  read_gate_checks
  echo "Review gate on $REPO ($MODE)"
  step_label
  step_merge
  step_secrets
  step_app
  step_rulesets
  if [ "$GAPS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "$GAPS missing."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "All set."
}

main "$@"
files..github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml:
# Routine PR review — binary 🔴/🟢 verdict
#
# The merge gate is one check, "Review gate", made through the Checks API on
# the PR head commit: a job's own check from the deep tier's comment-triggered
# run would attach to the default branch instead. Its decisions live in
# .github/scripts/review_gate.py and its settings in .github/review-gate.yml,
# both read from the base branch (or, when the base predates the gate, from
# the default branch), never from the PR:
#   • PR opens                         → in_progress
#   • Triage finds no reviewable files → success
#   • Routine verdict, no escalation   → success or failure
#   • Routine escalates                → in_progress until the deep verdict (claude.yml)
#   • A missing verdict or an error    → failure (fail closed)
# The check stores each tier's result in its external_id, stamped with the run
# step that wrote it, and every write is read back and redone if another one
# wiped it. So this workflow and claude.yml can finish in either order, or at
# the same moment, and the gate still holds both results.
#
# The older pair stays for branch rules that still require it: the
# "Evaluate review outcome" job reports either way, and `checks: two` in the
# settings keeps the "Claude On-Demand" check current too.
#
# Requires: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in repo secrets. Optional: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
# an org API key whose monthly credits pay for the routine review first.
#
# PERMANENT LIMITATION — claude-code-review.yml edits get no AI review:
#   The Anthropic Claude Code GitHub App validates that the workflow file on a PR's
#   head ref is byte-identical to the version on the default branch before granting
#   an OIDC-exchanged token, so the review action cannot run on a PR that edits this
#   file. Triage therefore never reviews this one file (.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml;
#   a .yaml twin would run as a separate workflow, so it is reviewed): a PR of only it and skippable
#   docs passes as non-reviewable. Edit it alone: mixed with reviewable files (claude.yml, the gate
#   script, .claude/), the review fails `Workflow validation failed` and the gate blocks, so those go
#   in their own PR first. Our own such PRs merge on two local reviews of the head commit; any other
#   PR waits for the maintainer's read.

name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    branches: [develop, main]

concurrency:
  # Cancel in-flight reviews when a newer commit lands on the same PR.
  group: claude-review-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  init-gate:
    name: Init review gate
    # Every PR gets the "Review gate" check on its head commit at once, so
    # branch protection has something to wait on, plus the gate settings for
    # the jobs below.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      checks: write
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      # The commit every job below reads the gate's files from: the base
      # commit, or the default branch's tip when the base predates the gate.
      gate_sha: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.gate_sha }}
      checks: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.checks }}
      routine_model: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.routine_model }}
      routine_effort: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.routine_effort }}
      routine_max_turns: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.routine_max_turns }}
      routine_fallback_model: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.routine_fallback_model || steps.settings.outputs.fallback_model }}
      routine_fallback_effort: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.routine_fallback_effort || steps.settings.outputs.fallback_effort }}
      runner_labels: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.runner_labels }}
      prescreen_dir: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.prescreen_dir }}
      # The project's own paths, for the pre-screen's file categories.
      always_review: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.triage_always_review }}
      escalate_paths: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.escalate_paths }}
      # The on/off switches (escalate.auto, prescreen.attribution); empty, from
      # a base script that predates them, counts as on.
      escalate_auto: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.escalate_auto }}
      prescreen_attribution: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.prescreen_attribution }}
      # Extra reviewer tools as a ready ",tool,tool" suffix for --allowedTools,
      # or empty. The script admits only Bash(...) without quotes, `$`,
      # backslashes or brackets inside, and Read, Grep, Glob.
      allowed_tools: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.reviewer_allowed_tools != '' && format(',{0}', steps.settings.outputs.reviewer_allowed_tools) || '' }}
    steps:
      # The gate's script and settings come from the base branch (or the
      # default branch, below): a PR must not be able to change how its own
      # review is judged.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github/scripts/
            .github/review-gate.yml
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      # A base branch from before the gate (an old release line) has no
      # script, and a PR into it could never pass. Those PRs take the gate
      # from the default branch's tip, which a PR cannot change either.
      - name: Check the base has the gate
        id: source
        run: |
          if [ ! -f .github/scripts/review_gate.py ]; then
            echo "::notice::The base commit has no review gate; using the gate from the default branch."
            echo "fallback=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        if: steps.source.outputs.fallback == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github/scripts/
            .github/review-gate.yml
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Read the gate settings
        id: settings
        run: |
          echo "gate_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if ! out=$(python3 -I .github/scripts/review_gate.py settings); then
            echo "::error::Bad review gate settings: $out"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$out" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Each run starts the routine tier over: until this run's verdict lands,
      # the gate waits, even on a re-run after an earlier verdict. Facts from
      # a deep review are kept. With `checks: two` the branch rules still
      # require the older pair, so a failed write to the new check must not
      # turn them red: it stays visible on this step only.
      - name: Create the Review gate check
        continue-on-error: ${{ steps.settings.outputs.checks == 'two' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          python3 -I .github/scripts/review_gate.py upsert --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" \
            --routine pending --order "${{ github.run_id }}.${{ github.run_attempt }}.0"

      - name: Create Claude On-Demand check at in_progress on PR HEAD SHA
        if: steps.settings.outputs.checks == 'two'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          # Idempotent: if the check already exists on this HEAD SHA, do
          # nothing. Re-running this job on a rerun_failed scenario must not
          # overwrite a deep-tier-set conclusion.
          EXISTING=$(gh api \
            "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Claude%20On-Demand&per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Claude On-Demand")] | first | .id // empty')
          if [ -n "$EXISTING" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Claude On-Demand check already exists on $HEAD_SHA (id=$EXISTING) — skipping create"
            exit 0
          fi

          gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs" -X POST \
            -F name="Claude On-Demand" \
            -F head_sha="$HEAD_SHA" \
            -F status="in_progress" \
            -F "output[title]=Waiting for routine review to evaluate" \
            -F "output[summary]=The routine review is evaluating whether deep-tier review is needed. This check will resolve to skipped (no escalation) or in_progress → success/failure (escalated to the deep tier)."
          echo "::notice::Created in_progress Claude On-Demand check on $HEAD_SHA"

  triage:
    name: Diff triage
    # The jobs after Init review gate run on the `runner` labels from the gate
    # settings; Init itself reads them, so it stays on a hosted runner, and
    # the fallback keeps Evaluate starting when Init failed.
    needs: init-gate
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init-gate.outputs.runner_labels || '["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      run_review: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.run_review }}
    # A self-hosted runner shares one workspace between jobs and workflows,
    # so this light checkout goes in a folder of its own: a sparse, partial
    # checkout of the workspace itself would leave other workflows' later
    # checkouts there sparse (and partial), missing most files.
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: .review-gate
    steps:
      # A PR checked out earlier in this workspace can leave `.review-gate`
      # behind, even as a link to another folder, which the checkout below
      # would then empty. Removing it takes the link, never its target.
      - name: Start the gate folder fresh
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: rm -rf .review-gate

      # The gate's script and settings from Init's commit (the base, or the
      # default branch's tip): which paths always get a review is a gate
      # setting, so a PR cannot change it for itself.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.gate_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: .review-gate
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github/scripts/
            .github/review-gate.yml
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Classify diff
        id: classify
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          PR=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO=${{ github.repository }}
          # The diff endpoint (`gh pr diff`) 406s past 300 files, so this uses
          # the paginated files API. A renamed file lists its old path too, so
          # moving a file out of a reviewable path is reviewed. A listing that
          # fails is passed on as incomplete, which the script reviews; so is
          # one that reaches the API's 3,000-file cap. Which files count, and
          # why this workflow never does, is in the script. A carriage
          # return or newline in a name becomes a space, so one name stays one
          # line: split, "docs/a.md<LF>.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml",
          # one .yml file, would read as a Markdown file and this workflow,
          # and skip the review. A space, unlike an escape, keeps "x.py<LF>" ending in .py
          # once the script strips the line. Leading whitespace (anything
          # Python's strip() removes) becomes "_", so
          # " .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml", a file in a folder
          # named " .github", can't strip down to this workflow's path.
          INCOMPLETE=""
          if ! gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty) | gsub("[\r\n]"; " ") | sub("^[\t\u000b\f\u001c-\u001f \u0085\u00a0\u1680\u2000-\u200a\u2028\u2029\u202f\u205f\u3000]+"; "_")' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed_files.txt"; then
            echo "::warning::The file listing failed; treating the diff as reviewable"
            INCOMPLETE="--incomplete"
          fi
          RESULT=$(python3 -I .github/scripts/review_gate.py triage "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed_files.txt" $INCOMPLETE \
            --file .github/review-gate.yml)
          echo "$RESULT"
          case "$RESULT" in
            '{"review": true}') echo "run_review=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
            '{"review": false}') echo "run_review=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
            *) echo "::error::Unexpected triage result"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

  project-triggers:
    name: Project triggers
    needs: [triage, init-gate]
    if: needs.triage.outputs.run_review == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init-gate.outputs.runner_labels || '["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    # The project's own deep-review triggers (escalate.* in the gate
    # settings), matched by the gate's own script from Init's commit (the
    # base, or the default branch's tip). This job runs none of
    # the PR's code, and none of the project's checks, which run in their own
    # job below: a check that runs the PR's code could otherwise rewrite the
    # result and skip the deep review. A failure here skips the review, which
    # fails the gate.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      escalate: ${{ steps.triggers.outputs.escalate }}
      context: ${{ steps.triggers.outputs.context }}
    steps:
      # A self-hosted runner shares one workspace between jobs and workflows.
      # The light jobs here check out into a folder of their own, but a
      # sparse or partial clone can still sit in the workspace (left by an
      # older version of this workflow, or another workflow). A full fetch
      # into a partial clone stays partial, and the diff below would then
      # fetch contents after the token is gone, which fails on a private
      # repo; a sparse one leaves most files out. So the full checkouts
      # start fresh from such a clone.
      - name: Drop a partial clone left by an earlier job
        run: |
          if [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get remote.origin.promisor 2>/dev/null)" = true ] \
              || [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get core.sparsecheckout 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; then
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.git"
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # As in Auto review: the PR's .gitattributes must not change the bytes.
      - name: Override the PR's git attributes
        run: |
          mkdir -p .git/info
          printf '%s\n' '* !diff -text !eol !working-tree-encoding !filter !ident' > .git/info/attributes
          git rm -rq --cached --ignore-unmatch . && git reset -q --hard

      - name: Match the project triggers
        id: triggers
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          GATE_SHA: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.gate_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gate="$RUNNER_TEMP/gate-base"
          mkdir -p "$gate"
          git show "$GATE_SHA:.github/scripts/review_gate.py" > "$gate/review_gate.py"
          if git cat-file -e "$GATE_SHA:.github/review-gate.yml" 2>/dev/null; then
            git show "$GATE_SHA:.github/review-gate.yml" > "$gate/review-gate.yml"
          fi
          # The same diff the pre-screen in Auto review reads. One name per
          # line: a carriage return or newline in a name becomes a space, so
          # "src/<LF>x.sql" can't split into names no glob matches, and bytes
          # that are not UTF-8 become \xNN escapes, so the script, which
          # decodes names strictly, never fails on a name.
          git -c core.quotePath=false diff --text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv \
            --ignore-submodules=none "origin/$BASE...HEAD" > "$gate/pr.diff"
          git diff -z --no-renames --name-only --ignore-submodules=none "origin/$BASE...HEAD" \
            | python3 -I -c 'import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"".join(n.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ").encode() + b"\n" for n in sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(b"\0") if n))' \
            > "$gate/files.txt"
          # A base branch from before the project triggers (a cascade into a
          # branch that lags main) has no escalate command; its settings
          # reject escalate.* outright, so no triggers can be set there.
          if grep -q 'review_gate.py escalate FILES DIFF' "$gate/review_gate.py"; then
            python3 -I "$gate/review_gate.py" escalate "$gate/files.txt" "$gate/pr.diff" \
              --file "$gate/review-gate.yml" > "$gate/escalate.json"
          else
            echo '{"escalate": false, "paths": [], "lines": []}' > "$gate/escalate.json"
          fi
          python3 -I - "$gate/escalate.json" <<'PYEOF'
          import json, os, sys
          esc = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))
          def cut(text, limit=300):
              return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit] + ' … (cut)'
          def code(text):
              # Indented code, so nothing in a PR line reads as markup.
              return ''.join('    ' + ln + '\n' for ln in text.splitlines()) or '    (no output)\n'
          parts = []
          if esc['escalate']:
              # The PR picks the paths and lines, so each is capped and so is
              # the list, to keep the listing short and its end visible.
              parts.append('Project deep-review triggers met (escalate.* in the gate settings):\n\n')
              parts += [f'- path: {cut(repr(p))}\n' for p in esc['paths'][:30]]
              if len(esc['paths']) > 30:
                  parts.append(f"- and {len(esc['paths']) - 30} more paths\n")
              if esc['lines']:
                  shown = '\n'.join(cut(ln) for ln in esc['lines'])
                  parts.append('- added lines matching the pattern:\n\n' + code(shown))
              parts.append('\n')
          context = ''.join(parts)
          if len(context) > 20000:
              context = context[:20000] + '\n(listing cut)\n'
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
              delim = 'EOF_' + os.urandom(16).hex()
              fh.write(f"escalate={'true' if esc['escalate'] else 'false'}\n")
              fh.write(f'context<<{delim}\n{context}\n{delim}\n')
          PYEOF

  project-checks:
    name: Project pre-screen
    needs: [triage, init-gate]
    if: needs.triage.outputs.run_review == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init-gate.outputs.runner_labels || '["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    # The project's own pre-screen checks (prescreen.dir in the gate
    # settings). The checks come from Init's commit (the base, or the
    # default branch's tip when the base predates the gate), and they run here, in
    # a job with no secrets and a read-only token, under an empty
    # environment with a home folder of its own: a check that runs the PR's
    # code reaches no review token and cannot set variables for the review
    # job's steps, though it can still rewrite this job's own report. On a
    # self-hosted runner that is not wiped between jobs, such a check can
    # also leave files or processes behind for the jobs that run there next,
    # the review included; keep checks that run the PR's code on hosted or
    # one-job runners. A failure here, a folder that commit does not have
    # included, skips the review, which fails the gate.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      context: ${{ steps.checks.outputs.context }}
    steps:
      # As in Project triggers: a full checkout starts from a fresh clone.
      - name: Drop a partial clone left by an earlier job
        if: needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir != ''
        run: |
          if [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get remote.origin.promisor 2>/dev/null)" = true ] \
              || [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get core.sparsecheckout 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; then
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.git"
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        if: needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir != ''
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # As in Auto review: the PR's .gitattributes must not change the bytes.
      - name: Override the PR's git attributes
        if: needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir != ''
        run: |
          mkdir -p .git/info
          printf '%s\n' '* !diff -text !eol !working-tree-encoding !filter !ident' > .git/info/attributes
          git rm -rq --cached --ignore-unmatch . && git reset -q --hard

      - name: Run the project checks
        id: checks
        if: needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir != ''
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          GATE_SHA: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.gate_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PRESCREEN_DIR: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gate="$RUNNER_TEMP/gate-checks"
          mkdir -p "$gate/checks" "$gate/out"
          # The diff and name list Project triggers reads.
          git -c core.quotePath=false diff --text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv \
            --ignore-submodules=none "origin/$BASE...HEAD" > "$gate/pr.diff"
          git diff -z --no-renames --name-only --ignore-submodules=none "origin/$BASE...HEAD" \
            | python3 -I -c 'import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"".join(n.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ").encode() + b"\n" for n in sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(b"\0") if n))' \
            > "$gate/files.txt"
          : > "$gate/checks.txt"
          git archive "$GATE_SHA" -- "$PRESCREEN_DIR" | tar -x -C "$gate/checks"
          find "$gate/checks/$PRESCREEN_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.sh' \) \
            -print0 | sort -z > "$gate/list"
          if [ ! -s "$gate/list" ]; then
            echo "::error::prescreen.dir '$PRESCREEN_DIR' holds no *.py or *.sh checks at the gate's commit $GATE_SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          while IFS= read -r -d '' check; do
            case "$check" in *.py) run=(python3 -I "$check") ;; *) run=(bash "$check") ;; esac
            status=0
            # RUNNER_TRACKING_ID lets the runner end what a check leaves
            # running when the job ends.
            env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$(mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/home.XXXXXX")" LANG=C.UTF-8 RUNNER_TRACKING_ID="${RUNNER_TRACKING_ID:-}" \
              timeout 300 "${run[@]}" "$gate/files.txt" "$gate/pr.diff" < /dev/null > "$gate/out/run" 2>&1 || status=$?
            printf '%s\t%s\n' "$status" "${check##*/}" >> "$gate/checks.txt"
            head -c 4000 "$gate/out/run" > "$gate/out/${check##*/}"
          done < "$gate/list"
          python3 -I - "$gate" <<'PYEOF'
          import os, sys
          gate = sys.argv[1]
          def code(text):
              # Indented code, so nothing in a check's output reads as markup.
              return ''.join('    ' + ln + '\n' for ln in text.splitlines()) or '    (no output)\n'
          parts = []
          rows = [ln.split('\t', 1) for ln in open(os.path.join(gate, 'checks.txt'), encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()]
          failed = [name for status, name in rows if status != '0']
          if rows:
              # The failed names lead, so a cut report still shows them.
              head = (f"## Project pre-screen violations ({len(failed)}: {', '.join(failed)}) — likely 🔴 unless you can refute each"
                      if failed else '## Project pre-screen checks: all passed')
              parts.append(head + '\n\n')
              for status, name in rows:
                  out = open(os.path.join(gate, 'out', name), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
                  # Indenting can grow output that is mostly line breaks, so
                  # each check's block is capped too.
                  block = code(out)
                  if len(block) > 5000:
                      block = block[:5000].rsplit('\n', 1)[0] + '\n    (output cut)\n'
                  parts.append(f'### {name}: exit {status}\n\n' + block + '\n')
          context = ''.join(parts)
          if len(context) > 20000:
              context = context[:20000] + '\n(report cut)\n'
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
              delim = 'EOF_' + os.urandom(16).hex()
              fh.write(f'context<<{delim}\n{context}\n{delim}\n')
          PYEOF

  claude-review:
    name: Auto review
    needs: [triage, init-gate, project-triggers, project-checks]
    if: needs.triage.outputs.run_review == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init-gate.outputs.runner_labels || '["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    # The model whose attempt wrote the verdict, for the gate's summary. The
    # job name and a green primary step cannot tell (the primary continues on
    # error). Models, effort and the turn cap come from the gate settings,
    # whose values the script checks against a strict pattern before any
    # step puts them on a command line.
    outputs:
      floor: ${{ steps.pre-screen.outputs.floor }}
      done: ${{ steps.repair.outputs.done }}
      reviewer: ${{ steps.credits-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' && format('{0} {1} (API credits)', needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_model, needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_effort) || steps.main-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' && format('{0} {1}', needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_model, needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_effort) || steps.backup-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' && format('{0} {1} (backup)', needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_fallback_model, needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_fallback_effort) || 'none' }}
    env:
      # What every review attempt returns (Step 3): the comment to post, and
      # the deep-review request ("" when it did not escalate).
      REVIEW_SCHEMA: '{"type":"object","properties":{"review":{"type":"string"},"deep_request":{"type":"string"}},"required":["review","deep_request"],"additionalProperties":false}'
      ROUTINE_REVIEW_PROMPT: |
        Review PR ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} in ${{ github.repository }}. What the project is, the invariants to verify and its extra escalation cases are in the project's review guide, under "Project review guide" at the end of the review context file (taken from the base branch, or from the default branch when the base predates the review gate, so the PR cannot change it). No such section means the project has no guide: review against the general rules below.

        **You work alone and this is a one-shot session: the moment you end your turn the session is over and nothing else runs.** Never delegate to helper agents or subagents, never schedule a wake-up, never "wait for" anything — a large diff is read file by file, in this turn, and your review is returned (Step 3) before you stop. A session that ends without it fails the PR's required check.

        ## Step 1 — Read the pre-screen report

        Read the review context file named on the first line of this prompt. It contains:
        - **Pre-screen violations** — mechanical rule-breakage already detected (AI-attribution markers in added lines). Each violation is likely 🔴 unless you can refute it from the diff.
        - **Pre-screen warnings** — likely issues you should judge (files the diff shows as binary, changed git attributes, etc.).
        - **Project pre-screen** — the project's own checks (`prescreen.dir` in the gate settings): a check that exited non-zero is a violation, likely 🔴 unless you can refute it; a line marked WARNING is for you to judge.
        - **Deep-review trigger surface** — if non-empty, Step 4 (the deep-review request) is mandatory. A project can turn automatic escalation off; the context then says so in place of this section.
        - **Project switches** — a section saying the project turned its AI-attribution check off, when it did.
        - **Categorized file lists** — architecture-critical files to READ first (including `.claude/` rules and skills, any `CLAUDE.md`, and the project's always-reviewed paths), then docs (scan only), then other code.
        - **Project review guide** — the project's own part of this prompt, from the base branch or, when the base predates the review gate, the default branch (absent when the project has none).

        The review runs on the base branch's config, so in your working folder the top-level `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude.json`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` and `.husky/` hold the base branch's copies: read the PR's version of any of those with `git show HEAD:<path>`, never with Read.

        Then read the PR diff once for the full context with local git: `git diff origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}...HEAD` (add `-- <path>` for one file). Not `gh pr diff`: it fails with HTTP 406 on PRs past 300 files, and the checkout you are in already has the full history. If the diff shows a file as binary (the pre-screen's `BINARY_IN_DIFF` names them), Read that file in full (for the base-config paths above, `git show HEAD:<path>` instead): a single NUL byte makes git hide a code file that way.

        **Trust the pre-screen.** Do NOT re-run the mechanical checks it already ran (the AI-attribution scan and the project's own checks). Read architecture-critical files in full (with `git show HEAD:<path>` for the base-config paths above); use `git diff` once for the diff; spend remaining turns on judgment work — architectural invariants, semantic regressions, contract drift. The allowlist is `gh pr view/diff/checks`, `gh issue view`, `gh run view/list`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show` and Read, sized for this contract — `cat`, `grep`, `wc`, `head` and `gh api` will be denied. You post nothing and apply no label: the workflow posts what you return.

        ## Step 2 — Architectural review
