        Read ONLY the files most likely to contain risk. Then expand outward if the architecture review surfaces a concern.

        **Project invariants:** verify the ones the review guide lists, in its order. Always verify, guide or not, unless the review context says the project turned this check off: no AI-attribution markers (`Co-Authored-By` lines naming an AI model, "Generated with" footers naming an AI tool, AI-vendor links) in added lines, commit messages or the PR body.

        ## Step 2.5 — Decide whether to escalate

        Escalation is *orthogonal* to the verdict — it's "deeper look requested," not a blocker. The verdict in Step 3 stays binary regardless.

        **Mark for escalation when ALL hold:**
        1. The concern is about correctness, not style.
        2. You can articulate a *specific* reason a deep-tier reviewer would catch what you cannot.
        3. You would not stake the merge on your own verdict for that concern.

        **Always mark when the pre-screen lists trigger paths** (the gate's own files, and the project's trigger paths from its gate settings). Escalation is not your call then: write the Step 4 request.

        **Always mark, too, when the diff includes anything the review guide lists under "Also escalate when the diff includes".**

        **Always mark, too, when the pre-screen report says a deep review is owed** (the PR already carries `needs-deep-review` from an earlier push). The deep check waits on every new head until a deep pass runs on it, so write the Step 4 request here too.

        **Do NOT mark for escalation:** docs, comments, formatting, naming nits, "consider extracting", pure refactors with no behavior change.

        **When the review context says automatic escalation is off for this project**, do not mark at all (the judgment and guide rules above do not apply): a person asks for every deep review. A deep review the context says is owed still stands.

        ## Step 3 — Return the review

        You do not post anything. End the session by returning your answer as structured output: `review` holds the full comment body (at most 60,000 characters), which the workflow posts on the PR as you wrote it (with a hidden line it adds under the first), and `deep_request` holds the Step 4 request, or an empty string when you did not escalate. The workflow posts the review first, then the request, so PR readers see the decision first.

        **Verdict is BINARY** — only 🔴 (Blocking) or 🟢 (LGTM). No middle ground.

        **⚠️ FAIL-CLOSED ENFORCEMENT — read before returning:** The gate reads the verdict from your review mechanically: your last line must open with 🔴 or 🟢 (any 🔴 on it blocks), unless a line that opens with 🔴 or `Blocking` after markup, or holds `Blocking` in any case right after a short label (`**Verdict:** blocking`), blocks first, wherever it sits. A comment whose last line opens with neither glyph blocks when the last line holding a glyph holds a 🔴, and is otherwise a MISSING verdict and the gate FAILS CLOSED. Do not count on any recovery from a different format. The emoji line is the contract. PRs with a bare `LGTM` line are not mergeable — the substance does not matter; the gate cannot tell.

        The review MUST:
        - Be titled `## Code Review — ${{ github.event.repository.name }}`
        - End with EXACTLY one of these as the FINAL line of the comment (no trailing prose after):
          - `🟢 LGTM`
          - `🔴 Blocking — must fix`

        **WRONG formats — never return any of these** (the gate reads some as a block or a missing verdict; the rest break the binary rule or the final-line format):
        - `LGTM` (missing 🟢 prefix — the most common mistake; do not do this)
        - `LGTM ✅` / `✅ LGTM` (wrong emoji — parser matches 🟢 only, not ✅)
        - `Blocking` or `Blocking — must fix` (missing 🔴 prefix)
        - `🟢 LGTM with caveats` / `🟢 LGTM — minor nit` (caveats forbidden; the binary rule below forces 🔴)
        - Any verdict line followed by trailing prose (`🟢 LGTM, ship it!` — must be the FINAL line, nothing after)
        - A 🟢 review that writes 🔴 or the word `Blocking` outside inline backticks (`### Blocking issues`, `**Blocking:** none`, `**🔴 …**`, `1. 🔴 Blocking …`): the gate blocks on lines like these wherever they sit, and on any 🔴 on the last line, backticks or not, so a 🟢 verdict line holds no 🔴 at all. A clean review writes neither except inside inline backticks on the same line; a line inside a fenced code block counts like any other

        **Self-check immediately before returning:** Look at the literal last line of your draft review. Does it start with `🟢` or `🔴`? If not — STOP, fix the line, re-check. The single most common review-quality failure on this repo is posting `LGTM` without the emoji, which blocks otherwise-clean PRs from merging.

        **BINARY VERDICT RULE:**
        - 🟢 LGTM ONLY when fully clean — zero caveats, zero minors, zero nits, zero "with caveats" headings.
        - 🔴 Blocking when ANY real finding exists, regardless of framing. "Minor nit" that suggests a real correctness improvement is 🔴. "All clear with caveats" is a contradiction — caveats make it 🔴.
        - DROP style preferences, micro-optimisations, future-proofing for hypothetical changes, "consider extracting" suggestions. Don't list them as non-blocking; just drop them.
        - "All clear on X" is allowed AS A SECTION HEADING. NEVER as the verdict line when other sections have findings.

        **MANDATORY when you marked the PR for escalation in Step 2.5 (auto-escalate OR uncertainty-based):** before the final verdict line, append a `### 🟡 Uncertainty surfaced — needs-deep-review requested` section. PR readers must see *what specifically* the deep pass is being asked to verify, not just *that* a deep pass was triggered. A deep-review request without a 🟡 section in the verdict above it is unmotivated and degrades the deep tier's signal quality — readers see only the trigger, not the rationale.

        Format (this block goes BEFORE the final verdict line; verdict stays binary 🟢/🔴):

        ```
        ### 🟡 Uncertainty surfaced — needs-deep-review requested

        - `<file:line>` — <what specifically concerns you about this change in 1 sentence>.
          **Why I am not confident:** <one sentence on the limit of your analysis — what you cannot fully verify from the diff/the files you read>.
          **What I want the deep tier to verify:** <one sentence naming the concrete check — invariant, contract, edge case>.
        - ...

        A depth-pass request follows in the next comment.
        ```

        For auto-escalated paths with no genuine uncertainty in your own read: still enumerate at least one concrete concern about THIS PR's changes on those paths — what regression a deep pass should mechanically rule out, what invariant could silently break. "Path is on the auto-escalate list" alone is NOT a sufficient 🟡 entry; the Step 4 request already says that. If you truly have nothing concrete to surface, that is signal that escalation is wrong for this PR — reconsider Step 2.5 and skip Step 4. Two exceptions, where Step 4 is never skipped: an owed deep review (name what changed since the last deep pass, and ask the deep tier to confirm the new head), and paths the pre-screen lists on the trigger surface (name what a deep pass should rule out on those paths).

        🟡 is NEVER the verdict line. A 🟢 verdict CAN carry a 🟡 section (genuinely-clean PR where the deep tier should still verify a specific concern). A 🔴 verdict CAN ALSO carry a 🟡 section (blocking findings plus uncertain ones for the deep tier). Binary verdict + optional 🟡 section are independent dimensions.

        ## Step 4 — IF you escalated in Step 2.5: write the deep-review request

        Only when Step 2.5 marked the PR for escalation; otherwise `deep_request` is an empty string. On every escalating run the workflow applies the `needs-deep-review` label and posts your request as a fresh comment, which starts the deep review. It MUST start with the literal words `@claude review this PR` (not in backticks, not under a heading) and follow this shape:

        ```
        @claude review this PR — depth pass on <focus>.

        <One-paragraph context: what the PR ships and why the risk surface is bigger than the diff suggests.>

        **Numbered invariants ranked by priority:**
        1. **<file:line>** — <invariant + how it could break>
        2. ...

        **Out of scope:** <list of intentional deferrals>

        If the diff shows a file as binary, Read that file in full in the working folder (for the base-config paths below, `git show HEAD:<path>` instead): a NUL byte or the PR's own .gitattributes can make a diff hide a code file that way. The review runs on the base branch's config, so in your working folder the top-level `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude.json`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` and `.husky/` hold the base branch's copies: read the PR's version of any of those with `git show HEAD:<path>`, never with Read.

        **Verdict format — BINARY, no in-between.** Same rule as the routine tier:
        - 🟢 LGTM ONLY when fully clean — zero caveats, zero minors, zero nits.
        - 🔴 Blocking when ANY real finding exists, regardless of framing.
        - DROP style preferences and micro-optimisations entirely.

        **⚠️ FAIL-CLOSED ENFORCEMENT — read before posting your verdict.** The deep tier's `Evaluate deep-tier verdict` step (in `claude.yml`) reads your completion comment mechanically — the SAME strict contract as the routine gate: your last line must open with 🔴 or 🟢 (any 🔴 on it blocks), unless a line that opens with 🔴 or `Blocking` after markup, or holds `Blocking` in any case right after a short label (`**Verdict:** blocking`), blocks first, wherever it sits. A comment whose last line opens with neither glyph blocks when the last line holding a glyph holds a 🔴, and is otherwise a MISSING verdict and fails the deep tier closed, blocking merge. Do not count on any recovery from a different format. The emoji line is the contract.

        **WRONG formats — never post any of these** (the deep gate reads some as a block or a missing verdict; the rest break the binary rule or the final-line format):
        - `LGTM` (missing 🟢 prefix — the most common mistake)
        - `LGTM ✅` / `✅ LGTM` (wrong emoji — the parser matches 🟢 only, not ✅)
        - `Blocking` / `Blocking — must fix` (missing 🔴 prefix)
        - `🟢 LGTM with caveats` / `🟢 LGTM — minor nit` (caveats forbidden; the binary rule forces 🔴)
        - Any verdict line followed by trailing prose (must be the FINAL line, nothing after)
        - A 🟢 review that writes 🔴 or the word `Blocking` outside inline backticks (`### Blocking issues`, `**Blocking:** none`, `**🔴 …**`, `1. 🔴 Blocking …`): the gate blocks on lines like these wherever they sit, and on any 🔴 on the last line, backticks or not, so a 🟢 verdict line holds no 🔴 at all. A clean review writes neither except inside inline backticks on the same line; a line inside a fenced code block counts like any other

        **Self-check before you finish:** look at the literal last line of your review. Does it start with 🟢 or 🔴? If not — STOP, fix it, re-check. A missing-emoji verdict fails the deep gate closed and blocks an otherwise-clean PR.

        **Output spec:** bullet-point findings ranked by severity with file:line citations. The verdict line is the FINAL line of the comment — `🟢 LGTM` or `🔴 Blocking — must fix`, no trailing prose.
        ```

        **CRITICAL — write the request even when a prior `@claude` comment exists on this PR.** The `claude.yml` deep-review workflow only fires on the `issue_comment` event for the CURRENT comment — it does not re-evaluate older comments when a new push lands. Every escalation posts a fresh comment, and it starts with the literal `@claude` token so both the workflow's `if: startsWith(body, '@claude review this PR')` condition AND the action's internal trigger detector evaluate true.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
      # Needed so the post-action step can PATCH the Claude On-Demand check
      # to in_progress when routine auto-escalates.
      checks: write
    steps:
      # As in Project triggers: a full checkout starts from a fresh clone.
      - name: Drop a partial clone left by an earlier job
        run: |
          if [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get remote.origin.promisor 2>/dev/null)" = true ] \
              || [ "$(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" config --get core.sparsecheckout 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; then
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.git"
          fi

      # No token left in .git/config, which the credits reviewer's worktree
      # shares: that reviewer reads PR content with a Read tool, and this
      # job's token can write checks. The fetches here are anonymous on a
      # public repo; the review action sets up its own auth.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # The PR's own .gitattributes must not change what the pre-screen and
      # the reviewer read: `-diff` or `binary` shows a file as "Binary files
      # differ", and working-tree-encoding, filter (git-lfs is installed on
      # the runner, and the PR controls .lfsconfig) or ident rewrite the
      # checked-out bytes.
      # .git/info/attributes outranks every .gitattributes and is shared by
      # the credits reviewer's worktree; the checkout is then redone under it.
      # A NUL byte still makes git call a file binary: the pre-screen warns.
      - name: Override the PR's git attributes
        run: |
          mkdir -p .git/info
          printf '%s\n' '* !diff -text !eol !working-tree-encoding !filter !ident' > .git/info/attributes
          git rm -rq --cached --ignore-unmatch . && git reset -q --hard

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # ── Pre-screen: deterministic Python checks over the diff ────────────────
      # Catches mechanical rule violations before the reviewer sees them. The reviewer then
      # trusts the report and spends turns on judgment work — NOT re-discovering
      # grep-able patterns. This is what makes the allowlist (a few `gh pr` read
      # commands, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show` and Read)
      # the right size: the reviewer doesn't need
      # `cat`/`grep`/`wc` because the pre-
      # screen already did that work.
      - name: Pre-screen PR diff
        id: pre-screen
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          GATE_SHA: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.gate_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          # From the Project pre-screen job: the project's own triggers count
          # like the trigger list below, and its report joins the context.
          PROJECT_ESCALATE: ${{ needs.project-triggers.outputs.escalate }}
          PROJECT_CONTEXT: ${{ needs.project-triggers.outputs.context }}${{ needs.project-checks.outputs.context }}
          ALWAYS_REVIEW: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.always_review }}
          ESCALATE_PATHS: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.escalate_paths }}
          PRESCREEN_DIR: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_dir }}
          ESCALATE_AUTO: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.escalate_auto }}
          PRESCREEN_ATTRIBUTION: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.prescreen_attribution }}
        run: |
          PR=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO=${{ github.repository }}

          # Local git, not `gh pr diff` — the API diff endpoint 406s past 300
          # files. The checkout above is fetch-depth 0, so the base branch is
          # present; three-dot (merge-base..HEAD) equals the PR's diff.
          # The name list uses --no-renames, so a renamed file's old path is
          # listed too and moving a file off the deep-review trigger list still
          # counts as touching it. The content diff keeps rename detection, so
          # a moved file's unchanged text is not read as added; its section is
          # keyed by the "rename to" path. -z lists every name raw;
          # without it git quotes names with accents, quotes or backslashes,
          # and a quoted name misses every trigger prefix. quotePath=false
          # keeps accented names raw in diff headers too; headers still quote
          # names with quotes, backslashes or control characters, which the
          # parser below unquotes.
          # --text, --no-ext-diff, --no-textconv: the checkout is the PR's, so
          # its .gitattributes could mark every file binary or route it through
          # a filter, and the scans below would read an empty diff.
          # --ignore-submodules=none: its .gitmodules could set `ignore = all`
          # on a submodule under a trigger folder and hide it from both lists.
          git -c core.quotePath=false diff --text --no-ext-diff --no-textconv \
            --ignore-submodules=none "origin/$BASE...HEAD" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr_diff.txt"
          git diff -z --no-renames --name-only --ignore-submodules=none \
            "origin/$BASE...HEAD" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed_files.txt"
          # Without --text, as the reviewer's own `git diff` runs: "-" counts
          # mark the files it will show as binary.
          git diff -z --no-renames --diff-filter=d --numstat "origin/$BASE...HEAD" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/numstat.txt"
          # The project's review guide, from the gate's commit (the base, or
          # the default branch when the base predates the gate) so the PR
          # cannot rewrite the guide its own review follows. No guide, no
          # section.
          git show "$GATE_SHA:.github/review-guide.md" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/review_guide.md" 2>/dev/null \
            || : > "$RUNNER_TEMP/review_guide.md"

          # The verdict floor for Evaluate: no review attempt of this run
          # starts before this moment, and a run this one replaced was
          # cancelled when this run was created, well before this job began.
          echo "floor=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # A deep review asked for on an earlier push is owed again on this
          # head: the deep check waits on every head while the label is on.
          LABELS=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")')
          case ",$LABELS," in *,needs-deep-review,*) export DEEP_OWED=1 ;; esac

          python3 -I - << 'PYEOF'
          import fnmatch
          import os
          import posixpath
          import re

          PR = os.environ.get('PR_NUMBER', '?')

          # surrogateescape keeps names that are not UTF-8 byte for byte, so
          # the diff's names equal the list's and open() still finds them.
          # newline='': only git's own \n ends a diff line. Text mode would turn
          # a lone \r inside an added line into a break, and the text after it
          # would lose its "+" and skip every scan.
          with open(os.path.join(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'], 'pr_diff.txt'), encoding='utf-8', errors='surrogateescape', newline='') as f:
              diff = f.read()
          with open(os.path.join(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'], 'changed_files.txt'), 'rb') as f:
              changed = [p.decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape') for p in f.read().split(b'\0') if p]

          GIT_ESCAPES = {'a': 7, 'b': 8, 't': 9, 'n': 10, 'v': 11, 'f': 12, 'r': 13, '"': 34, '\\': 92}

          def unquote_git_path(text):
              """Undo git's C-style quoting: named escapes and \\ooo octal bytes."""
              out, i = bytearray(), 0
              while i < len(text):
                  if text[i] == '\\' and re.fullmatch(r'[0-7]{3}', text[i + 1:i + 4]):
                      out.append(int(text[i + 1:i + 4], 8))
                      i += 4
                  elif text[i] == '\\' and text[i + 1:i + 2] in GIT_ESCAPES:
                      out.append(GIT_ESCAPES[text[i + 1]])
                      i += 2
                  else:
                      out += text[i].encode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape')
                      i += 1
              return out.decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape')

          def header_path(line):
              """The path in a `diff --git` header. Outside renames (keyed by
              rename_target) both sides name the same path, which splits even a
              name holding " b/"."""
              rest = line[len('diff --git '):]
              if rest.startswith('"'):
                  m = re.match(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', rest)
                  return unquote_git_path(m.group(1))[2:] if m else None
              size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2
              if rest[2 + size:] == ' b/' + rest[2:2 + size]:
                  return rest[2:2 + size]
              return None

          def shown(text):
              """A name or finding as one inert report line: control characters,
              bytes that are not UTF-8, backticks and backslashes are escaped,
              so a file name cannot start a line of its own in the report the
              reviewer trusts, and two names never show the same."""
              return ''.join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in '`\\' else escape(c) for c in text)

          def escape(c):
              """One character as an escape that names it exactly: a byte that
              is not UTF-8 (a surrogate after surrogateescape) as \\xNN, a
              backslash doubled, anything else by its code point as \\uNNNN or
              \\UNNNNNNNN."""
              n = ord(c)
              if 0xDC80 <= n <= 0xDCFF:
                  return f'\\x{n - 0xDC00:02x}'
              if c == '\\':
                  return '\\\\'
              return f'\\u{n:04x}' if n <= 0xFFFF else f'\\U{n:08x}'

          def rename_target(sec):
              """The new path of a renamed file, from its "rename to" line."""
              m = re.search(r'^rename to (.*)$', sec.split('\n@@', 1)[0], re.MULTILINE)
              if not m:
                  return None
              name = m.group(1)
              return unquote_git_path(name[1:-1]) if name.startswith('"') else name

          # Parse the diff into per-file added-line sections.
          violations = []   # rule-breakage — likely 🔴 unless the reviewer disagrees
          warnings   = []   # likely-needs-attention — reviewer judges

          per_file_added = {}
          for n, sec in enumerate(re.split(r'(?=^diff --git )', diff, flags=re.MULTILINE)):
              first = sec.split('\n', 1)[0]
              if not first.startswith('diff --git '):
                  continue
              fname = rename_target(sec) or header_path(first)
              # A header the parser cannot read is still scanned, never skipped.
              if fname is None:
                  fname = f'<unread diff header {n}>'
                  warnings.append(f'UNREAD_DIFF_HEADER: {first[:120]}')
              # Added lines are the "+" lines inside hunks; the "+++ b/" header
              # comes before the first "@@", so content opening with "++" counts.
              added, in_hunk = [], False
              for l in sec.split('\n'):
                  if l.startswith('@@'):
                      in_hunk = True
                  elif in_hunk and l.startswith('+'):
                      added.append(l[1:])
              per_file_added[fname] = added

          # ── Check 3: AI-attribution scan ─────────────────────────────────────
          # Scans ADDED lines for the AI-attribution patterns defined in
          # .claude/rules/git.md. The regexes are encoded in ai_pats below
          # (kept structural — readers consult ai_pats, not this comment,
          # to avoid the comment itself re-tripping the scanner on future
          # edits to this workflow file).
          # A project with prescreen.attribution off skips it.
          attribution = os.environ.get('PRESCREEN_ATTRIBUTION') != 'off'
          ai_pats = [
              re.compile(r'Co-Authored-By:\s*Claude', re.IGNORECASE),
              re.compile(r'Generated\s+with\s+\[?Claude\s+Code', re.IGNORECASE),
              re.compile(r'claude\.(?:com|ai)\b', re.IGNORECASE),
              re.compile(r'🤖\s*Generated', re.IGNORECASE),
          ] if attribution else []
          for fname, lines in per_file_added.items():
              for line in lines:
                  for pat in ai_pats:
                      if pat.search(line):
                          violations.append(f'AI_ATTRIBUTION: {fname}: {line.strip()[:120]}')
                          break

          # ── Check 4b: what the reviewer's diff hides ─────────────────────────
          # The workflow overrides the PR's attributes for this run, so a new
          # .gitattributes only matters once merged; the reviewer judges that.
          # A NUL byte still makes the reviewer's plain `git diff` print
          # "Binary files differ" for a code file, so those files are named.
          attrs = [f for f in changed if f.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] == '.gitattributes']
          if attrs:
              warnings.append(f'GITATTRIBUTES_CHANGED: {", ".join(attrs)} — overridden for this review; judge what the new attributes do once merged')
          with open(os.path.join(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'], 'numstat.txt'), 'rb') as f:
              stats = [p.decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape') for p in f.read().split(b'\0') if p]
          MEDIA = ('.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.gif', '.webp', '.ico', '.ttf', '.otf', '.woff', '.woff2')
          binary = [s[4:] for s in stats if s.startswith('-\t-\t') and not s[4:].lower().endswith(MEDIA)]
          if binary:
              warnings.append(f'BINARY_IN_DIFF: {", ".join(binary)} — git diff shows these as binary; Read each one in full (git show HEAD:<path> for the base-config paths)')

          # ── Check 5: Categorize files ────────────────────────────────────────
          # Read in full, never filed as low-risk docs: everything triage
          # always reviews (review_gate.ALWAYS_REVIEWED and the project's
          # triage.always_review, in any case), the project's deep-review
          # trigger paths (escalate.paths) and every workflow.
          ARCH = re.compile(r'^\.github/scripts/|^\.github/review-guide\.md$|(^|/)\.claude/|(^|/)CLAUDE(\.local)?\.md$'
                            # The CLI's own config, which every later review loads.
                            r'|(^|/)\.mcp\.json$|^\.claude\.json$|^\.husky/|^\.gitmodules$|^\.ripgreprc$', re.I)
          # The project's own checks (prescreen.dir) are part of the gate:
          # read in full and a deep-review trigger, like the gate's script.
          # Normalised as git names files: "./x", "x//y" and "x/./y" all mean
          # x/y. A folder of "." holds every file, so every file counts.
          CHECKS_DIR = os.environ.get('PRESCREEN_DIR', '').strip()
          CHECKS_DIR = posixpath.normpath(CHECKS_DIR).strip('/').casefold() if CHECKS_DIR else ''
          CHECKS_PREFIX = ('',) if CHECKS_DIR == '.' else (CHECKS_DIR + '/',) if CHECKS_DIR else ()
          # Matched as review_gate.py matches its path settings.
          OWN = [g.strip().casefold() for name in ('ALWAYS_REVIEW', 'ESCALATE_PATHS')
                 for g in os.environ.get(name, '').split(',') if g.strip()]
          def own_path(f):
              return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(f.casefold(), g + '*' if g.endswith('/') else g) for g in OWN)
          arch_critical, docs, other_code = [], [], []
          for f in changed:
              if (f.startswith('.github/workflows/') or ARCH.search(f) or own_path(f)
                      or f.casefold().startswith(CHECKS_PREFIX)):
                  arch_critical.append(f)
              elif f.endswith('.md'):
                  docs.append(f)
              else:
                  other_code.append(f)

          # ── Check 6: Deep-review trigger surface ─────────────────────────────
          # The gate's own files, in every project: its script, its settings,
          # the review guide, the review workflows and the project's checks
          # (CHECKS_PREFIX) decide what may merge. The project's own
          # trigger paths and patterns (escalate.*) come from the Project
          # triggers job as PROJECT_ESCALATE below.
          DEEP_PREFIXES = ('.github/scripts/', '.github/workflows/claude') + CHECKS_PREFIX  # claude.yml + claude-code-review.yml
          DEEP_FILES    = {'.github/review-gate.yml', '.github/review-guide.md'}
          # Matched in any case, like triage: a case-insensitive checkout puts
          # ".GitHub/Scripts/" in .github/scripts/. With escalate.auto off the
          # routine review starts no deep review (the project's triggers then
          # match nothing either); a deep review already owed still stands.
          auto_escalate = os.environ.get('ESCALATE_AUTO') != 'off'
          deep_paths = [
              f for f in changed
              if f.casefold().startswith(DEEP_PREFIXES) or f.casefold() in DEEP_FILES
          ] if auto_escalate else []
          # The Repair step applies the label itself when these paths changed,
          # so the deep review is owed whatever the reviewer does.
          project_deep = auto_escalate and os.environ.get('PROJECT_ESCALATE') == 'true'
          project_context = os.environ.get('PROJECT_CONTEXT', '')
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as gh_out:
              gh_out.write(f"deep_paths={'true' if deep_paths or project_deep else 'false'}\n")

          # ── Write the review context ─────────────────────────────────────────
          # backslashreplace is a backstop: shown() escapes every name first,
          # so a byte that is not UTF-8 should never reach the writer.
          with open(os.path.join(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'], 'review_context.md'), 'w', encoding='utf-8', errors='backslashreplace') as out:
              out.write(f'# Pre-screen report for PR #{PR}\n\n')

              if violations:
                  out.write(f'## Pre-screen violations ({len(violations)}) — likely 🔴 unless you can refute each\n\n')
                  for v in violations:
                      out.write(f'- `{shown(v)}`\n')
                  out.write('\n')
              else:
                  out.write('## Pre-screen violations: none\n\n')

              if warnings:
                  out.write(f'## Pre-screen warnings ({len(warnings)}) — reviewer judges\n\n')
                  for w in warnings:
                      out.write(f'- `{shown(w)}`\n')
                  out.write('\n')

              deep_owed = os.environ.get('DEEP_OWED') == '1'
              if deep_paths or deep_owed or project_deep:
                  out.write('## Deep-review trigger surface — auto-escalation REQUIRED (Step 4)\n\n')
                  if deep_owed:
                      out.write('This PR already carries `needs-deep-review` from an earlier push, so a deep review is owed on this head too: the deep check waits until one runs. You MUST write the Step 4 request (`deep_request`), no exceptions; name in it what changed since the last deep pass.\n\n')
                  if deep_paths or project_deep:
                      out.write('These paths are on the deep-review trigger list, so escalation is decided already, not by your judgment. The workflow applies `needs-deep-review` itself and posts your Step 4 request (`deep_request`), so write it in full, no exceptions, naming what a deep pass should rule out on these paths:\n\n')
                      for p in deep_paths:
                          out.write(f'- `{shown(p)}`\n')
                      if project_deep:
                          out.write("- the project's own triggers, listed in the next section\n")
                  out.write('\n')
              elif not auto_escalate:
                  out.write('## Deep-review escalation: off for this project (Step 2.5 and Step 4 skipped)\n\n'
                            'Do not mark this PR for escalation: in this project a person asks for every deep review.\n\n')
              else:
                  out.write('## Deep-review trigger surface: none (Step 4 skipped)\n\n')
              if not attribution:
                  out.write('## AI-attribution check: off for this project\n\n'
                            'Skip the always-verify attribution invariant.\n\n')
              # The project's report comes first-hand from the Project triggers
              # and Project pre-screen jobs, which format every PR-derived line
              # as indented code.
              if project_context.strip():
                  out.write(project_context.rstrip('\n') + '\n\n')

              out.write('## Architecture-critical files (READ THESE)\n\n')
              if arch_critical:
                  for f in arch_critical:
                      out.write(f'- `{shown(f)}`\n')
              else:
                  out.write('_(none)_\n')
              out.write('\n')

              out.write('## Docs / markdown changes (low-risk, scan only)\n\n')
              if docs:
                  for f in docs:
                      out.write(f'- `{shown(f)}`\n')
              else:
                  out.write('_(none)_\n')
              out.write('\n')

              out.write('## Other code changes\n\n')
              if other_code:
                  for f in other_code:
                      out.write(f'- `{shown(f)}`\n')
              else:
                  out.write('_(none)_\n')

              # Merged text from the gate's commit, so it goes in as written.
              with open(os.path.join(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP'], 'review_guide.md'), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                  guide = f.read()
              if guide.strip():
                  out.write('\n## Project review guide (from the base or default branch)\n\n')
                  out.write(guide.rstrip('\n') + '\n')

          print(f'Pre-screen complete. Violations={len(violations)}, Warnings={len(warnings)}, Deep-trigger={len(deep_paths)}, Deep-owed={deep_owed}, Arch-critical={len(arch_critical)}')
          PYEOF

          echo "--- review_context.md ---"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/review_context.md"

      # One job-private copy of the newest CLI release, so the credits run and
      # the action's review run the same version. The version is read when the
      # job runs, from the channel the official installer reads, and then
      # installed exactly, so those steps and the log name one version. When
      # the lookup or the install fails, the credits run is skipped and the
      # action's review falls back to the CLI it bundles. The backup runs on
      # the stable release (see below).
      - name: Install Claude Code
        id: claude-cli
        # Each download has its own limit too, so a stalled host ends in the
        # warnings below rather than at the step's limit.
        timeout-minutes: 30
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER: "1"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CLI_VERSION=""
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if CLI_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest); then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::warning::Could not look up the newest Claude Code release: the review runs on the action's own CLI; the backup tries the stable release"
              exit 1
            fi
            sleep $((attempt * 20))
          done
          CLI_VERSION=$(printf '%s' "$CLI_VERSION" | tr -d '[:space:]')
          if [[ ! "$CLI_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::warning::The release channel returned no version: the review runs on the action's own CLI; the backup tries the stable release"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Newest Claude Code release: $CLI_VERSION"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 https://claude.ai/install.sh | timeout 300 bash -s -- "$CLI_VERSION"; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::warning::Claude Code $CLI_VERSION install failed three times: the review runs on the action's own CLI; the backup tries the stable release"
              exit 1
            fi
            # The install host answers bursts with HTTP 429: back off longer.
            sleep $((attempt * 20))
          done
          src="$HOME/.local/share/claude/versions/$CLI_VERSION"
          if [ ! -x "$src" ]; then
            src="$(readlink -f "$HOME/.local/bin/claude" || true)"
          fi
          dest="$RUNNER_TEMP/claude-cli/claude"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
          if ! cp "$src" "$dest"; then
            echo "::warning::Claude Code $CLI_VERSION left no binary to copy: the review runs on the action's own CLI; the backup tries the stable release"
            exit 1
          fi
          chmod +x "$dest"
          installed="$(timeout -k 10 60 "$dest" --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' || true)"
          if [ "$installed" != "$CLI_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::warning::expected Claude Code $CLI_VERSION, got '$installed': the review runs on the action's own CLI; the backup tries the stable release"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::notice::The credits run and the main review run Claude Code $installed"
          echo "path=$dest" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$installed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # ── First attempt: the plan's monthly API credits ─────────────────────
      # The org API key pays for a plain `claude -p` run from its monthly
      # credits; a run made through the review action is refused them
      # ("Credit balance is too low"). Like every attempt, it posts nothing:
      # it returns its review as structured output, which the check below
      # reads and "Post the review" posts. No answer the gate can read (no
      # key, credits or the workspace cap spent, an API error, a broken run)
      # leaves the review to the action steps below, which run on the
      # subscription.
      - name: Run Claude Code Review on the API credits
        id: claude-review-credits
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          CLI: ${{ steps.claude-cli.outputs.path }}
          DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER: "1"
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_model }}
          EFFORT: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_effort }}
          MAX_TURNS: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.routine_max_turns }}
          EXTRA_TOOLS: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.allowed_tools }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::notice::No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret: the review runs on the subscription"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$CLI" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Claude Code was not installed: the review runs on the subscription"
            exit 1
          fi

          # The CLI acts on config it finds in its working folder (hooks,
          # settings, MCP servers), and the PR controls those files. Like the
          # review action, run it in a copy of the checkout whose config comes
          # from the base branch; the checkout itself stays as it is for the
          # fallback steps. `--setting-sources user --strict-mcp-config` below
          # also keeps the restored project settings from loading.
          wt="$RUNNER_TEMP/credits-review"
          bot_token=""
          cleanup() {
            if [ -n "$bot_token" ]; then
              GH_TOKEN="$bot_token" timeout -k 10 120 gh api -X DELETE /installation/token >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            fi
            git worktree remove --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          }
          trap cleanup EXIT
          git worktree add --quiet --detach "$wt" HEAD
          for p in .claude .mcp.json .claude.json .gitmodules .ripgreprc CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.local.md .husky; do
            rm -rf "${wt:?}/$p"
            git -C "$wt" checkout "origin/$BASE_REF" -- "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
          done

          # The reviewer reads the PR with the review app's token, as the
          # action's reviewer does, never with the job's token (that one can
          # write checks). It is handed back when the step ends.
          oidc=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=claude-code-github-action" \
            | python3 -I -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["value"])') || oidc=""
          echo "::add-mask::$oidc"
          if [ -n "$oidc" ]; then
            bot_token=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $oidc" \
              https://api.anthropic.com/api/github/github-app-token-exchange \
              | python3 -I -c 'import json, sys; d = json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get("token") or d.get("app_token") or "")') || bot_token=""
          fi
          if [ -z "$bot_token" ]; then
            echo "::warning::The bot token exchange returned no token: the review runs on the subscription"
            exit 1

      # deep-review request. No attempt can post, so a crashed, hung or
      # re-posting attempt never leaves a second verdict; the gate reads this
      # comment. Posted as the review app (claude[bot]), as Evaluate expects.
      - name: Post the review
        id: post
        if: steps.credits-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' || steps.main-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' || steps.backup-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          DEEP_PATHS: ${{ steps.pre-screen.outputs.deep_paths }}
          ESCALATE_AUTO: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.escalate_auto }}
          FLOOR: ${{ steps.pre-screen.outputs.floor }}
          STAGE: ${{ steps.credits-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' && 'credits' || steps.main-answer.outputs.ok == 'yes' && 'main' || 'backup' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Every GitHub call gets a limit, so a stalled one fails the step
          # instead of holding the job.
          gh() { timeout -k 10 120 gh "$@"; }
          # Three tries, 10 s and 20 s apart: one network blip must not throw
          # away a finished review.
          retry() {
            local n
            for n in 1 2 3; do
              if "$@"; then return 0; fi
              [ "$n" = 3 ] || sleep $((n * 10))
            done
            return 1
          }
          review="$RUNNER_TEMP/$STAGE-review.md"
          request="$RUNNER_TEMP/$STAGE-deep-request.md"
          # This run attempt's mark, hidden in each comment under its first
          # line (the check step put it in the review, the body it checked):
          # a try whose post landed but whose answer was lost is found by it,
          # so a retry never posts a second copy.
          mark="<!-- review-run: $GITHUB_RUN_ID-$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT -->"
          # Posts a comment once: the created_at of the marked comment, found
          # or new. $1 is the file, $2 the comment kind for the mark.
          post_once() {
            local body="$1" at
            if [ "$2" != review ]; then
              body="$RUNNER_TEMP/post-$2.md"
              { head -n 1 "$1"; printf '\n%s %s -->\n' "${mark% -->}" "$2"; tail -n +2 "$1"; } > "$body"
            fi
            at=$(GH_TOKEN="$bot_token" gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" \
              | jq -rs --arg m "${mark% -->} $2 -->" '[add[] | select(.user.login == "claude[bot]") | select((.body // "") | contains($m))] | first | .created_at // ""') || return 1
            if [ -z "$at" ]; then
              at=$(GH_TOKEN="$bot_token" gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" -F "body=@$body" --jq .created_at) || return 1
            fi
            printf '%s' "$at"
          }
          # Sets bot_token: run in this shell, never in a $(...), so its mask
          # lines reach the runner and not the token.
          token_once() {
            local oidc
            bot_token=""
            oidc=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
              "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=claude-code-github-action" \
              | python3 -I -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["value"])') || return 1
            echo "::add-mask::$oidc"
            bot_token=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 60 -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $oidc" \
              https://api.anthropic.com/api/github/github-app-token-exchange \
              | python3 -I -c 'import json, sys; d = json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get("token") or d.get("app_token") or "")') || bot_token=""
            [ -n "$bot_token" ]
          }
          bot_token=""
          if ! retry token_once; then
            echo "::error::The bot token exchange failed three times, so the review cannot be posted; re-run this job"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::add-mask::$bot_token"
          trap 'GH_TOKEN="$bot_token" gh api -X DELETE /installation/token >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
          # GitHub's own time for the comment: the repair step's `done`, the
          # end of the window Evaluate reads, is never before it, whatever the
          # runner's clock says.
          posted_at=$(retry post_once "$review" review)
          echo "posted_at=$posted_at" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "::notice::Posted the $STAGE review"
          # The floor, the start of Evaluate's window, is the runner's time:
          # a runner clock ahead of GitHub's would put the review before it,
          # and Evaluate would read no verdict. Fail loudly instead.
          if [[ "$posted_at" < "$FLOOR" ]]; then
            echo "::error::GitHub dates the review ($posted_at) before this run's floor ($FLOOR): the runner's clock is ahead of GitHub's, so Evaluate cannot see it. Fix the runner's clock, then re-run all jobs."
            exit 1
          fi

          # A deep review is owed when the reviewer asked for one (a request,
          # or, with escalation on, the Step 3 escalation heading's words
          # anywhere in the review: a loud label beats a dropped request), the
          # diff is on the trigger list, or the PR already carries the label
          # (or, with escalation on, the label read fails).
          owed=no
          if [ -s "$request" ] || [ "$DEEP_PATHS" = true ]; then
            owed=yes
          fi
          if [ "$ESCALATE_AUTO" != off ] && grep -qi "needs-deep-review requested" "$review"; then
            owed=yes
          fi
          if labels=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")'); then
            case ",$labels," in *",needs-deep-review,"*) owed=yes ;; esac
          elif [ "$ESCALATE_AUTO" != off ]; then
            owed=yes
          fi
          if [ "$owed" != yes ]; then
            exit 0
          fi
          retry gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/labels" -X POST -f "labels[]=needs-deep-review" >/dev/null
          # The deep tier's action path has no prompt of its own: the request
          # is its brief. With none from the reviewer, or one that does not
          # start the deep workflow, the fixed brief goes first.
          brief="$RUNNER_TEMP/deep-request.md"
          start=$(head -c 200 "$request" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
          if [[ "$start" == "@claude review this pr"* ]]; then
            cp "$request" "$brief"
          else
            cat > "$brief" <<'BRIEF'
          @claude review this PR — depth pass on the whole diff.

          A deep review is owed on this head (the reviewer asked for one, the diff is on the trigger list, or the PR already carries needs-deep-review). The review above lists its concerns in its `needs-deep-review requested` section when it has one; either way, review the whole diff adversarially.

          If the diff shows a file as binary, Read that file in full in the working folder (for the base-config paths below, `git show HEAD:<path>` instead): a NUL byte or the PR's own .gitattributes can make a diff hide a code file that way. The review runs on the base branch's config, so in your working folder the top-level `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude.json`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` and `.husky/` hold the base branch's copies: read the PR's version of any of those with `git show HEAD:<path>`, never with Read.

          **Verdict format — BINARY, no in-between.** Same rule as the routine tier:
          - 🟢 LGTM ONLY when fully clean — zero caveats, zero minors, zero nits.
          - 🔴 Blocking when ANY real finding exists, regardless of framing.
          - DROP style preferences and micro-optimisations entirely.

          **⚠️ FAIL-CLOSED ENFORCEMENT — read before posting your verdict.** The deep tier's `Evaluate deep-tier verdict` step (in `claude.yml`) reads your completion comment mechanically — the SAME strict contract as the routine gate: your last line must open with 🔴 or 🟢 (any 🔴 on it blocks), unless a line that opens with 🔴 or `Blocking` after markup, or holds `Blocking` in any case right after a short label (`**Verdict:** blocking`), blocks first, wherever it sits. A comment whose last line opens with neither glyph blocks when the last line holding a glyph holds a 🔴, and is otherwise a MISSING verdict and fails the deep tier closed, blocking merge. Do not count on any recovery from a different format. The emoji line is the contract.

          **WRONG formats — never post any of these** (the deep gate reads some as a block or a missing verdict; the rest break the binary rule or the final-line format):
          - `LGTM` (missing 🟢 prefix — the most common mistake)
          - `LGTM ✅` / `✅ LGTM` (wrong emoji — the parser matches 🟢 only, not ✅)
          - `Blocking` / `Blocking — must fix` (missing 🔴 prefix)
          - `🟢 LGTM with caveats` / `🟢 LGTM — minor nit` (caveats forbidden; the binary rule forces 🔴)
          - Any verdict line followed by trailing prose (must be the FINAL line, nothing after)
          - A 🟢 review that writes 🔴 or the word `Blocking` outside inline backticks (`### Blocking issues`, `**Blocking:** none`, `**🔴 …**`, `1. 🔴 Blocking …`): the gate blocks on lines like these wherever they sit, and on any 🔴 on the last line, backticks or not, so a 🟢 verdict line holds no 🔴 at all. A clean review writes neither except inside inline backticks on the same line; a line inside a fenced code block counts like any other

          **Self-check before you finish:** look at the literal last line of your review. Does it start with 🟢 or 🔴? If not — STOP, fix it, re-check. A missing-emoji verdict fails the deep gate closed and blocks an otherwise-clean PR.

          **Output spec:** bullet-point findings ranked by severity with file:line citations. The verdict line is the FINAL line of the comment — `🟢 LGTM` or `🔴 Blocking — must fix`, no trailing prose.
          BRIEF
            if [ -s "$request" ]; then
              printf '\n\n**The reviewer added:**\n\n' >> "$brief"
              cat "$request" >> "$brief"
            fi
          fi
          retry post_once "$brief" request >/dev/null
          echo "::notice::Applied needs-deep-review and posted the deep-review request"

      # ── Escalation: repair the label, resolve Claude On-Demand ───────────
      # Runs AFTER the review steps so it sees the label they applied. The
      # Evaluate job reads that label as "a deep review was asked for".
      # A trigger comment from this run counts as escalation even when its
      # label is missing: the step applies the label. So does a diff on the
      # trigger list, whatever the reviewer returned.
      # With `checks: two`, the older Claude On-Demand check (created at
      # in_progress by init-gate) then moves to one of two states:
      #   • No needs-deep-review label → conclusion=skipped (passes branch
      #     protection; visually clear "this didn't run").
      #   • Label applied → status=in_progress with updated title "Deep
      #     review in progress" — branch protection blocks merge until
      #     claude.yml PATCHes to success/failure.
      - name: Repair the deep-review label and resolve Claude On-Demand
        id: repair
        if: always() && steps.claude-review-credits.conclusion != 'cancelled' && steps.claude-review.conclusion != 'cancelled'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CHECKS: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.checks }}
          DEEP_PATHS: ${{ steps.pre-screen.outputs.deep_paths }}
          POSTED_AT: ${{ steps.post.outputs.posted_at }}
        run: |
          PR="${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          # Every review attempt has ended: Evaluate reads the routine verdict
          # only from comments posted between the floor and this moment, so a
          # re-run of Evaluate alone cannot pick up a later comment. Never
          # before GitHub's time for the posted review, so a runner clock
          # behind GitHub's still keeps it in the window.
          DONE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
          if [[ "$POSTED_AT" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$ ]] && [[ "$POSTED_AT" > "$DONE" ]]; then
            DONE="$POSTED_AT"
          fi
          echo "done=$DONE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # "Post the review" applies the label with the request. If a
          # deep-review trigger was posted this run but the label is
          # missing, apply the label here, so a failed label call can never
          # mark the deep check skipped while the deep review runs.
          RUN_STARTED_AT=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" --jq '.run_started_at')
          if [ -z "$RUN_STARTED_AT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Could not resolve this run's run_started_at, so whether the reviewer escalated is unknown"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Fetched on its own line so a failed request stops the step (the
          # runner's bash has -e but no pipefail) instead of reading as zero.
          COMMENTS=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments")
          TRIGGERS=$(printf '%s' "$COMMENTS" \
            | jq -s -r --arg ts "$RUN_STARTED_AT" \
                '[.[][] | select(.user.login == "claude[bot]") | select(.created_at >= $ts) | select((.body // "") | ascii_downcase | startswith("@claude review this pr"))] | length')
          LABELS=$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")')
          if [ "$TRIGGERS" -gt 0 ] && ! echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "needs-deep-review"; then
            gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/labels" -X POST -f "labels[]=needs-deep-review" >/dev/null
            echo "::warning::A deep-review trigger was posted this run without the label; applied needs-deep-review"
            LABELS="$LABELS,needs-deep-review"
          fi
          # Trigger-list paths make the deep review owed by rule, not by the
          # reviewer's judgment: apply the label whatever the reviewer did. The
          # backstop below then fails this run if no deep review was asked for.
          if [ "$DEEP_PATHS" = "true" ] && ! echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "needs-deep-review"; then
            gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/labels" -X POST -f "labels[]=needs-deep-review" >/dev/null
            echo "::warning::The diff touches deep-review trigger paths and the label was missing; applied needs-deep-review"
            LABELS="$LABELS,needs-deep-review"
          fi

          # Backstop: while the label is on, the deep check waits on this head
          # until a deep run reports. With no deep-review request since this
          # run started and no deep result yet, nothing would ever start one:
          # fail loudly instead of a silent wait. Only requests claude.yml acts
          # on count: the reviewer's, or one from someone with write access.
          # A re-run fixes it: the pre-screen makes the reviewer ask again.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "needs-deep-review"; then
            # claude.yml also starts on review bodies and review comments, and
            # Actions' startsWith ignores case, so all three count, lower-cased.
            # Each fetch on its own line, so a failed one stops the step.
            REVIEWS=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/reviews")
            REVIEW_COMMENTS=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/comments")
            ASKERS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s' "$COMMENTS" "$REVIEWS" "$REVIEW_COMMENTS" \
              | jq -s -r --arg ts "$RUN_STARTED_AT" \
                  '[.[][] | select((.created_at // .submitted_at // "") >= $ts) | select((.body // "") | ascii_downcase | startswith("@claude review this pr")) | .user.login] | unique | .[]')
            REQUESTED=no
            # Read line by line, never word-split: the bot's login ends in
            # "[bot]", a glob that would match files the PR checkout holds.
            while IFS= read -r ASKER; do
              [ -n "$ASKER" ] || continue
              if [ "$ASKER" = "claude[bot]" ]; then
                REQUESTED=yes
                break
              fi
              # A failed lookup (a bot or deleted account) counts as no access.
              PERM=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$ASKER/permission" --jq .permission) || PERM=none
              case "$PERM" in
                admin|maintain|write) REQUESTED=yes; break ;;
              esac
            done <<< "$ASKERS"
            GATE_STATE=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Review%20gate&per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Review gate")] | max_by(.id) | .external_id // ""')
            if [ "$REQUESTED" = no ] && { [ -z "$GATE_STATE" ] || echo "$GATE_STATE" | grep -q "deep=none"; }; then
              echo "::error::needs-deep-review is on, but no deep review was requested this run and none has reported on $HEAD_SHA. Re-run this workflow so the reviewer requests it."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

          if [ "$CHECKS" != "two" ]; then
            exit 0
          fi
          CHECK_ID=$(gh api \
            "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Claude%20On-Demand&per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Claude On-Demand")] | first | .id // empty')
          if [ -z "$CHECK_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::Claude On-Demand check not found on $HEAD_SHA — init-gate must have skipped or failed"
            exit 1
          fi

          # ── Terminal-state guard ──────────────────────────────────────────
          # If claude.yml's Evaluate step already PATCHed the check to a
          # terminal state (success or failure), do NOT overwrite. Scenarios:
          # (a) maintainer manually @claude-triggered before routine
          # completed and the deep review finished first; (b) "Re-run all jobs" on the
          # routine workflow after the deep review has set a terminal state. The
          # `skipped` and `in_progress` states ARE safe to overwrite —
          # they're set by this routine workflow, not by claude.yml's
          # authoritative Evaluate step.
          # One read for status, conclusion and title: separate reads could
          # straddle the deep run's final write and see none of its marks.
          EXISTING=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID")
          EXISTING_STATUS=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.status')
          EXISTING_CONCLUSION=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.conclusion // ""')
          EXISTING_TITLE=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.output.title // ""')
          if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" = "completed" ] && { [ "$EXISTING_CONCLUSION" = "success" ] || [ "$EXISTING_CONCLUSION" = "failure" ]; }; then
            echo "::notice::Claude On-Demand check $CHECK_ID is at terminal state ($EXISTING_CONCLUSION) — the deep tier has spoken; routine Resolve will not overwrite"
            exit 0
          fi
          # A deep review asked for by hand may be running with no label. It
          # shows on the Review gate (escalated=yes, no deep result yet) and,
          # in case that write failed, on this check itself: claude.yml marks
          # it "Deep review running". Skipping the check then would let both
          # required checks pass while that review runs.
          GATE_NOW=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Review%20gate&per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Review gate")] | max_by(.id) | .external_id // ""')
          RUNNING=no
          case ";$GATE_NOW;" in
            *";escalated=yes;deep=none;"*) RUNNING=yes ;;
          esac
          if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" = "in_progress" ] && [ "$EXISTING_TITLE" = "Deep review running" ]; then
            RUNNING=yes
          fi
          REASON=""
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "needs-deep-review"; then
            REASON="needs-deep-review applied. Waiting for the deep-tier verdict (claude.yml will PATCH this check on completion)."
          elif [ "$RUNNING" = yes ]; then
            REASON="A deep review was asked for on this head and has not reported yet (claude.yml will PATCH this check on completion). If no deep run is alive, ask again with a comment starting with \`@claude review this PR\`."
          fi
          # Keep claude.yml's "Deep review running" marker while that review
          # runs, so every later routine pass on this head still sees it.
          TITLE="Deep review in progress"
          if [ "$RUNNING" = yes ]; then
            TITLE="Deep review running"
          fi
          # Already marked by a running deep review: leave it to that review,
          # whose final write may land at any moment and must not be undone.
          if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" = "in_progress" ] && [ "$EXISTING_TITLE" = "Deep review running" ]; then
            echo "::notice::A deep review is running on $HEAD_SHA; Claude On-Demand stays as it marked it"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ -n "$REASON" ]; then
            gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID" -X PATCH \
              -F status="in_progress" \
              -F "output[title]=$TITLE" \
              -F "output[summary]=$REASON"
            echo "::notice::Set Claude On-Demand check $CHECK_ID to in_progress (escalated)"
          else
            gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID" -X PATCH \
              -F status="completed" \
              -F conclusion="skipped" \
              -F "output[title]=Deep review skipped — no escalation" \
              -F "output[summary]=Routine review found no uncertainty warranting deep-tier escalation. To request a deep review anyway, post a comment starting with \`@claude review this PR — depth pass on <focus>\`."
            echo "::notice::Set Claude On-Demand check $CHECK_ID to skipped (no escalation)"
          fi

  evaluate-review-outcome:
    name: Evaluate review outcome
    needs: [init-gate, triage, claude-review]
    # Runs on every PR event, including non-reviewable docs-only PRs:
    # `always()` keeps it firing when `claude-review` is skipped by triage
    # (or by a failed Project pre-screen, which reads as a routine error).
    # It reports the routine result twice:
    #   • into the "Review gate" check, through the script, which adds the
    #     deep tier's result when there is one (claude.yml writes that part);
    #   • as this job's own pass or fail, the older "Evaluate review outcome"
    #     check, routine tier only:
    #       1. Triage classified the diff as non-reviewable → pass (and, with
    #          `checks: two`, Claude On-Demand → skipped).
    #       2. Routine review job didn't reach success → fail (action errored,
    #          OIDC tripped, workflow-validation skip, runner crash).
    #       3. Routine verdict comment missing or 🔴 → fail.
    #       4. Routine 🟢 → pass.
    if: always()
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.init-gate.outputs.runner_labels || '["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
      # The Review gate check, and with `checks: two` the non-reviewable path's
      # PATCH of Claude On-Demand to skipped (otherwise it would stay at
      # in_progress on docs-only PRs and block the merge).
      checks: write
    # As in Diff triage: the light checkout gets a folder of its own.
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: .review-gate
    steps:
      # As in Diff triage: a `.review-gate` a PR left behind goes first.
      - name: Start the gate folder fresh
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: rm -rf .review-gate

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.gate_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: .review-gate
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: .github/scripts/
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      # Gathers the facts; never fails on a verdict, so the next two steps
      # both see them. If this step dies, both read the routine tier as an
      # error, whatever outputs it wrote before dying (the runner keeps them).
      - name: Read the routine verdict
        id: routine
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          PR_NUMBER="${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"

          # Bad settings or a dead triage: fail closed. Triage's outputs are
          # untrusted when it died (an empty run_review reads as non-reviewable).
          if [ "${{ needs.init-gate.result }}" != "success" ] || [ "${{ needs.triage.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            printf 'triage=reviewable\nroutine=error\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.triage.outputs.run_review }}" != "true" ]; then
            echo "triage=skip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "triage=reviewable" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "${{ needs.claude-review.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "routine=error" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # ── Stale-verdict floor (current-run correlation) ─────────────────
          # `claude-review.result == success` reflects job-level exit status —
          # it's possible for the action to exit clean WITHOUT posting a
          # verdict comment (hit --max-turns, gh failure, refusal). A naive
          # newest-comment pick would then read the PRIOR push's stale 🟢,
          # fail-opening the gate. Only comments posted at or after this run's
          # review job began count: not the run's creation, since a run this
          # one replaced can still post during its cancellation.
          FLOOR="${{ needs.claude-review.outputs.floor }}"
          DONE="${{ needs.claude-review.outputs.done }}"
          if [ -z "$FLOOR" ] || [ -z "$DONE" ]; then
            echo "::error::The routine review's start or end time is unknown — refusing to evaluate verdict without both bounds"
            echo "routine=error" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # --paginate is mandatory: the comments endpoint defaults to 30 per
          # page, so on a long-thread PR the verdict lands on a later page.
          # Title-tolerant marker: the reviewer does not reliably reproduce the
          # exact `## Code Review — <repository name>` heading (observed
          # `**Code Review - …**` and a heading-less `Code Review — …`), so it
          # matches the stable phrase with any separator, but only where the
          # comment starts: the deep-review request and a deep run's tracking
          # comment can name the heading further down and quote both verdict
          # formats, and both are posted after the verdict. The script reads
          # only claude[bot]'s comments that match, never a deep-review comment.
          # Lines like `**🔴 …**`, `- 🔴 x` or `**Verdict:** blocking` block
          # wherever they sit; otherwise the last line, under the review
          # action's footer, must open with 🔴 or 🟢, and any 🔴 on it blocks
          # (the script lists exactly which lines count).
          gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/all-comments.json"
          jq -s --arg end "$DONE" '[.[][] | select(.created_at <= $end)]' "$RUNNER_TEMP/all-comments.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/comments.json"
          # A dot in the repository name is escaped so it matches only itself.
          MARKER_NAME=$(printf '%s' "${REPO#*/}" | sed 's/\./\\./g')
          VERDICT=$(python3 -I .github/scripts/review_gate.py verdict --since "$FLOOR" --tier routine \
            --marker "^[\\s#*_]*Code Review[^a-zA-Z]+$MARKER_NAME" < "$RUNNER_TEMP/comments.json")
          echo "$VERDICT"
          ROUTINE=$(printf '%s' "$VERDICT" | jq -r .verdict)
          RECOVERED=$(printf '%s' "$VERDICT" | jq -r '.recovered // empty')
          if [ -n "$RECOVERED" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Routine verdict read from a malformed comment: $RECOVERED"
          fi
          LABELS=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")')
          # The verdict is written last, so it never stands without the label
          # read that tells whether a deep review was asked for.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "needs-deep-review"; then
            echo "escalated=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "routine=$ROUTINE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # With `checks: two`, a failed write to the not-yet-required gate must
      # not turn this job, the older required check, red.
      - name: Update the Review gate
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.checks == 'two' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          READ: ${{ steps.routine.outcome }}
          TRIAGE: ${{ steps.routine.outputs.triage || 'reviewable' }}
          ROUTINE: ${{ steps.routine.outputs.routine || (steps.routine.outputs.triage != 'skip' && 'error' || '') }}
          ESCALATED: ${{ steps.routine.outputs.escalated }}
          REVIEWER: ${{ needs.claude-review.outputs.reviewer }}
        run: |
          if [ "$READ" != "success" ]; then
            TRIAGE=reviewable
            ROUTINE=error
          fi
          ARGS=(--triage "$TRIAGE")
          if [ -n "$ROUTINE" ]; then ARGS+=(--routine "$ROUTINE"); fi
          if [ "$ESCALATED" = "true" ]; then ARGS+=(--escalated); fi
          if [ -n "$REVIEWER" ]; then ARGS+=(--note "Routine reviewer: $REVIEWER."); fi
          python3 -I .github/scripts/review_gate.py upsert --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" \
            --order "${{ github.run_id }}.${{ github.run_attempt }}.1" "${ARGS[@]}"

      - name: Resolve routine verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REVIEWER: ${{ needs.claude-review.outputs.reviewer }}
          CHECKS: ${{ needs.init-gate.outputs.checks }}
          TRIAGE: ${{ steps.routine.outputs.triage }}
          ROUTINE: ${{ steps.routine.outputs.routine }}
        run: |
          REPO="${{ github.repository }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"

          if [ "${{ steps.routine.outcome }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::Reading the routine verdict failed — failing closed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.init-gate.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::Init review gate did not succeed (bad gate settings?) — failing closed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.triage.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::Triage did not succeed (result: ${{ needs.triage.result }}) — refusing to trust its outputs, failing closed"
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "$TRIAGE" = "skip" ]; then
            echo "✅ Triage classified diff as non-reviewable — gate auto-passes"
            if [ "$CHECKS" != "two" ]; then
              exit 0
            fi
            CHECK_ID=$(gh api \
              "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Claude%20On-Demand&per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Claude On-Demand")] | first | .id // empty')
            if [ -n "$CHECK_ID" ]; then
              # Terminal-state guard (symmetric with the Resolve step's guard):
              # if a maintainer manually @claude-triggered on a docs-only PR
              # and the deep review set the check to success/failure, a routine re-run
              # must not overwrite that authoritative verdict with skipped.
              # One read for all three fields, as in the Resolve step.
              EXISTING=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID")
              EXISTING_STATUS=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.status')
              EXISTING_CONCLUSION=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.conclusion // ""')
              EXISTING_TITLE=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING" | jq -r '.output.title // ""')
              if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" = "completed" ] && { [ "$EXISTING_CONCLUSION" = "success" ] || [ "$EXISTING_CONCLUSION" = "failure" ]; }; then
                echo "::notice::Claude On-Demand check $CHECK_ID is at terminal state ($EXISTING_CONCLUSION) — will not overwrite with skipped"
                exit 0
              fi
              # Same for a deep review asked for by hand that is still running:
              # the Review gate holds escalated=yes with no deep result yet, or
              # (if that write failed) this check reads "Deep review running".
              GATE_NOW=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?check_name=Review%20gate&per_page=100" \
                --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Review gate")] | max_by(.id) | .external_id // ""')
              RUNNING=no
              case ";$GATE_NOW;" in
                *";escalated=yes;deep=none;"*) RUNNING=yes ;;
              esac
              if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" = "in_progress" ] && [ "$EXISTING_TITLE" = "Deep review running" ]; then
                RUNNING=yes
              fi
              if [ "$RUNNING" = yes ]; then
                # Rewrite only a check the deep run has not marked itself (say,
                # one a racing skip left skipped): a marked one is that run's,
                # and its final write must not be undone.
                if [ "$EXISTING_STATUS" != "in_progress" ] || [ "$EXISTING_TITLE" != "Deep review running" ]; then
                gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID" -X PATCH \
                  -F status="in_progress" \
                  -F "output[title]=Deep review running" \
                  -F "output[summary]=A deep review was asked for on this head and has not reported yet (claude.yml will PATCH this check on completion). If no deep run is alive, ask again with a comment starting with \`@claude review this PR\`." >/dev/null
                fi
                echo "::notice::A deep review is running on $HEAD_SHA — leaving Claude On-Demand at in_progress"
                exit 0
              fi
              gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs/$CHECK_ID" -X PATCH \
                -F status="completed" \
                -F conclusion="skipped" \
                -F "output[title]=Deep review skipped — diff non-reviewable" \
                -F "output[summary]=Triage classified the diff as non-reviewable (only the routine review workflow, and Markdown, images and fonts outside the always-reviewed paths). Deep review not applicable."
              echo "::notice::Set Claude On-Demand check $CHECK_ID to skipped (non-reviewable diff)"
            else
              # Self-heal: init-gate didn't create the check (Checks API 5xx,
              # permission propagation delay on a fresh bind, runner blip).
              # Create it directly here so docs-only PRs don't stall in
              # branch-protection's "Expected" state on transient infra
              # failures. The reviewable path's Resolve step exits 1 in the
              # same scenario (clearer signal there); the non-reviewable path
              # self-heals to preserve the fast-path ~30-second auto-merge UX.
              echo "::warning::Claude On-Demand check missing on $HEAD_SHA — creating directly (init-gate may have failed)"
              gh api "repos/$REPO/check-runs" -X POST \
                -F name="Claude On-Demand" \
                -F head_sha="$HEAD_SHA" \
                -F status="completed" \
                -F conclusion="skipped" \
                -F "output[title]=Deep review skipped — diff non-reviewable" \
                -F "output[summary]=Triage classified the diff as non-reviewable. init-gate did not create the check earlier in this run (Checks API blip or permission propagation delay); this step recovered by creating it directly."
              echo "::notice::Created Claude On-Demand check directly at skipped (recovery path)"
            fi
            exit 0
          fi

          case "$ROUTINE" in
            pass)
              echo "Routine review verdict: 🟢 LGTM, from $REVIEWER" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              echo "::notice::Routine review verdict: 🟢 LGTM (reviewer: $REVIEWER)"
              exit 0 ;;
            block)
              echo "Routine review verdict: 🔴 Blocking, from $REVIEWER" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              echo "::error::Routine review verdict: 🔴 Blocking — must fix (reviewer: $REVIEWER)" ;;
            missing)
              echo "::error::No routine verdict this run: no review comment, or one whose last line does not open with 🔴/🟢 (max-turns hit, gh failure, or refusal; reviewer: $REVIEWER)" ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Claude review job did not complete successfully (result: ${{ needs.claude-review.result }})" ;;
          esac
          exit 1
files..github/workflows/claude.yml:
# On-demand deep review
# Filters on body SIGNATURE (`@claude review this PR`), not author. Mirrors
# GameProject's proven shape: the routine review's structured trigger comment
# (claude-code-review.yml Step 4.B) is posted with the review app's
# installation token, not GITHUB_TOKEN (whose comments start no workflow) —
# author = `claude[bot]`. So is the action's own progress comment. Body content
# distinguishes the two cleanly:
#   • Trigger comment body STARTS with `@claude review this PR — depth pass`.
#   • Progress comment body is `Claude Code is working…` and contains
#     `@claude` only inside backticks — never the literal substring
#     `@claude review this PR`.
#
# Merge gate participation: this workflow writes the deep result into the
# "Review gate" check on the PR head commit through the shared script
# (.github/scripts/review_gate.py, taken from the PR's base commit, or from the
# default branch when the base predates the gate), which
# combines it with the routine result stored on the same check. See the
# comment block in claude-code-review.yml. With `checks: two` in the gate
